sentences.zh: 劉頌

translations.literal: Liu Song.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 劉頌，字子雅，廣陵人，漢廣陵厲王胥之後也。

translations.literal: Liu Song, courtesy name Ziya, was a man of Guangling, a descendant of the Han Prince Li of Guangling, Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song, courtesy name Ziya, came from Guangling and traced his line to Prince Li of Guangling under the Han, Liu Xu.

sentences.zh: 世為名族。

translations.literal: For generations they were a famous clan.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had ranked among the great houses of the region.

sentences.zh: 同郡有雷、蔣、谷、魯四姓，皆出其下，時人為之語曰「雷、蔣、谷、魯，劉最為祖。」

translations.literal: In the same commandery were the four surnames Lei, Jiang, Gu, and Lu; all came out below them, and people of the time made a saying for them: "Lei, Jiang, Gu, Lu—Liu is most the ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: Guangling also boasted the four houses of Lei, Jiang, Gu, and Lu, yet all stood beneath the Lius, and a local rhyme ran, "Lei, Jiang, Gu, and Lu bow to Liu as their elder stock."

sentences.zh: 父觀，平陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Guan was Administrator of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Guan had served as prefect of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 頌少能辨物理，為時人所稱。

translations.literal: Song in youth was able to discriminate things' principles, and was praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Liu Song could reason to the root of affairs and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，舉秀才，皆不就。

translations.literal: He was investigated as filial and incorrupt, recommended as flourishing talent, all did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Though nominated as filial and incorrupt and as a flourishing talent, he declined each summons.

sentences.zh: 文帝辟為相府掾，奉使於蜀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen summoned him as a clerk in the chancellery and sent him on mission to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen appointed him a staff clerk in the princely chancellery and dispatched him on embassy to Shu.

sentences.zh: 時蜀新平，人饑土荒，頌表求振貸，不待報而行，由是除名。

translations.literal: At that time Shu was newly pacified; people starved and the land lay waste. Song memorialized requesting relief loans, without awaiting reply acted, thereby was removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had only just been pacified: the people were starving and the fields lay waste. Liu Song submitted an urgent plea for grain relief and distributed aid before imperial approval arrived, for which he was struck from office.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，拜尚書三公郎，典科律，申冤訟。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was appointed Gentlemen of the Three Excellencies in the Masters of Writing, in charge of statutes and regulations, extending wronged lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne Liu Song was named a Three Excellencies gentleman in the Masters of Writing, charged with statutes and codes and with redressing unjust suits.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to gentleman attendant of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 咸寧中，詔頌與散騎郎白褒巡撫荊、揚，以奉使稱旨，轉黃門郎。

translations.literal: In the Xianning era an edict ordered Song together with Cavalier Gentleman Bai Bao to tour and comfort Jing and Yang; because carrying out the mission matched the intent, he was transferred to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianning the court sent Liu Song and Bai Bao, cavalier gentleman, on an inspection tour of Jingzhou and Yangzhou. The mission pleased the throne, and Liu Song was moved to gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 遷議郎，守廷尉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Consultant and acted as Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to consultant and served as acting commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令史扈寅非罪下獄，詔使考竟，頌執據無罪，寅遂得免，時人以頌比張釋之。

translations.literal: At that time Masters of Writing clerk Hu Yin entered prison without crime; an edict ordered him interrogated to the end. Song held proof of innocence, and Yin was able to be spared. People of the time compared Song to Zhang Shizhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Yin, a clerk of the Masters of Writing, was jailed on a false charge and the emperor ordered a full inquest, Liu Song proved his innocence and secured his release. Contemporaries likened him to the Han jurist Zhang Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 在職六年，號為詳平。

translations.literal: In office six years, he was titled thorough and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Six years in the post earned him a reputation for meticulous fairness.

sentences.zh: 會滅吳，諸將爭功，遣頌校其事，以王渾為上功，王浚為中功。

translations.literal: When Wu was destroyed, the various generals disputed merit; Song was sent to examine the matter, taking Wang Hun as upper merit and Wang Jun as middle merit.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Wu the generals wrangled over credit. The court charged Liu Song with adjudicating their claims; he ranked Wang Hun first and Wang Jun second.

sentences.zh: 帝以頌持法失理，左遷京兆太守，不行，轉任河內。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Song upholding law missed principle, demoted him to Administrator of Jingzhao; he did not go, was transferred to serve in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor faulted Liu Song for misapplying the law and demoted him to prefect of Jingzhao. Liu Song never took up that post and was reassigned instead to Henei.

sentences.zh: 臨發，上便宜，多所納用。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure, he submitted convenient proposals, many of which were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out he offered practical policy recommendations, many of which the throne accepted.

sentences.zh: 郡界多公主水碓，遏塞流水，轉為浸害，頌表罷之，百姓獲其便利。

translations.literal: Within the commandery boundary were many princesses' water trip-hammers that dammed and blocked flowing water, turning into inundation harm; Song memorialized to abolish them, and the hundred surnames obtained their convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Princess-owned water mills across the commandery had choked the streams and caused flooding. Liu Song had them shut down by edict, to the great relief of the commoners.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon he left office on account of mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除淮南相。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he was appointed Chancellor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning term ended he was named chancellor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 在官嚴整，甚有政績。

translations.literal: In office he was strict and orderly, and had very good administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He ran a tight administration and compiled an impressive record.

sentences.zh: 舊修芍陂，年用數萬人，豪強兼併，孤貧失業，頌使大小戮力，計功受分，百姓歌其平惠。

translations.literal: Formerly repairing Shao Lake annually used several tens of thousands of men; powerful families annexed labor, orphans and poor lost employment. Song caused great and small to join strength, reckoned merit and received shares, and the hundred surnames sang his even kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The old Shao Lake works had drafted tens of thousands each year while magnates monopolized labor and left widows and paupers destitute. Liu Song made every household share the burden by measured shifts and fair rationing, and the people praised his equity.

sentences.zh: 頌在郡，上疏曰：臣昔忝河內，臨辭受詔：「卿所言悉要事，宜大小數以聞。

translations.literal: While Song was in the commandery, he submitted a memorial: Your servant once held the post of Administrator of Henei; on taking leave he received an edict: "What you speak of are all important matters; you should report them, great and small, in number.
translations.idiomatic: While administering the commandery Liu Song memorialized: Your servant once served as Administrator of Henei and, on taking leave, received an edict: "What you report concerns matters of weight; you should keep me informed of them, great and small.

sentences.zh: 恆苦多事，或不能悉有報，勿以為疑。」

translations.literal: I am constantly troubled by many affairs and may not be able to reply to all in full; do not take this as cause for doubt."
translations.idiomatic: I am constantly burdened with affairs and may not be able to answer everything in full; do not doubt me on that account."

sentences.zh: 臣受詔之日，喜懼交集，益思自竭，用忘其鄙，願以螢燭，增暉重光。

translations.literal: On the day your servant received the edict, joy and fear mingled; he thought all the more to exhaust himself, thereby forgetting his lowliness, wishing with a firefly or candle to add light to the heavy radiance.
translations.idiomatic: On the day your servant received that edict, joy and fear mingled together; he resolved all the more to give his utmost, forgetting his own unworthiness, hoping that like a firefly or candle he might add a little light to your greater brilliance.

sentences.zh: 到郡草具所陳如左，未及書上，會臣嬰丁天罰，寢頓累年，今謹封上前事。

translations.literal: On reaching the commandery he drafted what he would present as below, but before he could submit it in writing, your servant suffered Heaven's punishment in bereavement and lay ill for years; now he respectfully seals and presents the earlier matter.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the commandery he drafted the memorial below, but before he could submit it, your servant was struck by Heaven's punishment in bereavement and lay ill for years; he now respectfully seals and presents that earlier submission.

sentences.zh: 臣雖才不經國，言淺多違，猶願陛下垂省，使臣微誠得經聖鑒，不總棄于常案。

translations.literal: Although your servant's talent is not equal to governing the state and his words are shallow and often at odds, he still wishes Your Majesty to look down and examine, so that his slight sincerity may pass the sage mirror and not be wholly cast aside among ordinary documents.
translations.idiomatic: Though your servant's talent falls short of governing the realm and his words are shallow and often wide of the mark, he still hopes Your Majesty will deign to examine them, so that this slight sincerity may reach your sage discernment and not be wholly discarded among routine papers.

sentences.zh: 如有足采，冀補萬一。

translations.literal: If there is anything worth adopting, he hopes it may supply one part in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: If anything here is worth adopting, he hopes it may prove of some small use.

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書，開啟土宇，以支百世，封建戚屬，咸出之籓，夫豈不懷，公理然也。

translations.literal: Prostrate, he has seen the edict opening the realm and extending it to support a hundred generations, enfeoffing imperial kin and sending them all out to the frontier domains; who would not approve? Public reason is so.
translations.idiomatic: Prostrate, he has seen the edict opening the realm to support generations yet to come, enfeoffing imperial kinsmen and sending them all to frontier domains; who would not approve? Public reason demands it.

sentences.zh: 樹國全制，始成於今，超秦、漢、魏氏之局節，紹五帝三代之絕跡。

translations.literal: The complete system of establishing states is now first achieved, surpassing the patterns of Qin, Han, and Wei, and continuing the broken traces of the Five Emperors and Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The full system of establishing feudal states is now first brought to completion, surpassing the arrangements of Qin, Han, and Wei and renewing the broken line of the Five Emperors and Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 功被無外，光流後裔，巍巍盛美，三五之君殆有慚德。

translations.literal: Merit covers all without, glory flows to later generations; lofty and grand in splendor and beauty, the lords of the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors would almost feel ashamed of their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Its merit extends everywhere abroad, its glory flows to later generations; in loftiness and splendor it is so grand that even the rulers of the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors might feel ashamed before it.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 彼因自然而就之，異乎絕跡之後更創之。

translations.literal: They achieved it by following what was natural, unlike creating anew after the traces had been broken off.
translations.idiomatic: They achieved it by following what was already natural, unlike creating anew after the old line had been broken.

sentences.zh: 雖然，封幼稚皇子于吳、蜀，臣之愚慮，謂未盡善。

translations.literal: Even so, enfeoffing young princes in Wu and Shu, in your servant's foolish thought, is not yet fully good.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, in your servant's humble view, enfeoffing young princes in Wu and Shu is not yet the best course.

sentences.zh: 夫吳、越剽輕，庸、蜀險絕，此故變釁之所出，易生風塵之地。

translations.literal: Wu and Yue are swift and light; Yong and Shu are perilous and remote—these are places where disturbances arise and dust of turmoil easily rises.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Yue are swift and restless; Yong and Shu are perilous and remote—places where disturbances arise and turmoil easily flares.

sentences.zh: 且自吳平以來，東南六州將士更守江表，此時之至患也。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the pacification of Wu, the generals and soldiers of the six southeastern provinces have in rotation guarded the lands south of the Yangzi—this is the greatest affliction of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since Wu was pacified, the generals and soldiers of the six southeastern provinces have rotated in guarding the lands south of the Yangzi—the greatest affliction of the age.

sentences.zh: 又內兵外守，吳人有不自信之心，宜得壯主以鎮撫之，使內外各安其舊。

translations.literal: Again, with inner troops guarding the outer lands, the people of Wu lack confidence; there should be a strong lord to pacify and soothe them, so that inner and outer each rest secure in their old ways.
translations.idiomatic: Again, with troops from within guarding lands abroad, the people of Wu lack confidence in the regime; a strong prince should be placed there to pacify and reassure them, so that within and without each may rest secure in accustomed ways.

sentences.zh: 又孫氏為國，文武眾職，數擬天朝，一旦堙替，同於編戶。

translations.literal: Again, under the Sun house there was a state; civil and military offices in multitude matched the imperial court; in one morning they were buried and replaced, becoming the same as registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Again, under the Sun house there had been a state whose civil and military offices in multitude rivaled the imperial court; in a single morning that order was buried and its people reduced to ordinary registered households.

sentences.zh: 不識所蒙更生之恩，而災困逼身，自謂失地，用懷不靖。

translations.literal: They do not recognize the grace of renewed life they have received, yet disaster and hardship press upon them; they deem themselves dispossessed and therefore harbor unrest.
translations.idiomatic: They do not recognize the grace of renewed life they have received; disaster and hardship press upon them, they deem themselves dispossessed, and therefore harbor unrest.

sentences.zh: 今得長王以臨其國，隨才授任，文武並敘，士卒百役不出其鄉，求富貴者取之於國內。

translations.literal: Now if an elder prince were obtained to oversee their state, appointing men according to talent, ordering civil and military alike, so that soldiers and corvée laborers need not leave their native districts and those seeking wealth and rank obtain them within the state—
translations.idiomatic: If an elder prince were now placed over that region, appointing men according to talent and ordering civil and military offices alike, so that soldiers and corvée laborers need not leave their native districts and those seeking wealth and rank obtain them within the domain—

sentences.zh: 內兵得散，新邦乂安，兩獲其所，於事為宜。

translations.literal: inner troops could be dispersed, the new domain would be well governed, both sides would gain what they need—in the matter this would be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: —inner troops could be dispersed, the new domain would be well governed, and both sides would gain what they need; in the matter this would be fitting.

sentences.zh: 宜取同姓諸王年二十以上人才高者，分王吳、蜀。

translations.literal: One should take princes of the same surname who are over twenty and of high talent and divide Wu and Shu among them as domains.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of the imperial surname who are over twenty and of high talent should be chosen and given separate domains in Wu and Shu.

sentences.zh: 以其去近就遠，割裂土宇，令倍於舊。

translations.literal: Because they leave what is near and take what is far, the land should be divided and their territories made twice what they were before.
translations.idiomatic: Because they would leave what is near and take what is far, their lands should be divided and their territories doubled in size.

sentences.zh: 以徙封故地，用王幼稚，須皇子長乃遣君之，於是無晚也。

translations.literal: By transferring enfeoffment to the old lands and using young princes, one need only wait until the imperial sons are grown before sending them as lords—then there would be no delay.
translations.idiomatic: By transferring enfeoffments to the old domains and using young princes for now, one need only wait until the imperial sons are grown before sending them as lords—then there would be no delay.

sentences.zh: 急所須地，交得長主，此事宜也。

translations.literal: Where land is urgently needed, one would at once obtain an elder lord; in this matter it would be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Where land is urgently needed, an elder prince would at once be obtained; in this matter the course is fitting.

sentences.zh: 臣所陳封建，今大義已舉，然餘眾事，儻有足采，以參成制，故皆並列本事。

translations.literal: What your servant has presented on enfeoffment has now set forth the great principle; yet as to the remaining many matters, if any are worth adopting to help complete the system, he therefore lists the original matters together.
translations.idiomatic: What your servant has presented on enfeoffment has now set forth the great principle; yet regarding the remaining matters, if any are worth adopting to help complete the system, he therefore lists them together with the original points.

sentences.zh: 臣聞：不憚危悔之患，而願獻所見者，盡忠之臣也；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: one who does not fear the peril of regret and yet wishes to offer what he sees is a fully loyal minister;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that one who does not fear the peril of regret and yet offers what he sees is a fully loyal minister;

sentences.zh: 垂聽逆耳，甘納苦言者，濟世之君也。

translations.literal: one who listens to what grates on the ear and willingly accepts bitter words is a ruler who saves the age.
translations.idiomatic: and one who listens to what grates on the ear and willingly accepts bitter counsel is a ruler who saves the age.

sentences.zh: 臣以期運，幸遇無諱之朝。

translations.literal: Your servant, by the fortune of the age, has luckily encountered a court without taboo.
translations.idiomatic: By the fortune of the age, your servant has been blessed to serve in a court where frank speech is not forbidden.

sentences.zh: 雖嘗抗疏陳辭，泛論政體，猶未悉所見，指言得失，徒荷恩寵，不異凡流。

translations.literal: Although he has once submitted a memorial and set forth words, broadly discussing the body of government, he has still not fully stated what he sees and pointed out gain and loss; he has merely received grace and favor, no different from the common run.
translations.idiomatic: Although he has once submitted a memorial broadly discussing the body of government, he has still not fully stated what he sees or pointed out what succeeds and fails; he has merely received grace and favor, no different from the common run.

sentences.zh: 臣竊自愧，不盡忠規，無以上報，謹列所見如左。

translations.literal: Your servant privately feels ashamed that he has not fully offered loyal counsel and has nothing with which to repay favor; he respectfully lists what he sees as below.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is privately ashamed that he has not fully offered loyal counsel and has nothing with which to repay your grace; he respectfully lists what he sees below.

sentences.zh: 臣誠未自許所言必當，然要以不隱所懷為上報之節。

translations.literal: Your servant truly does not assure himself that what he says must be correct, yet he takes not hiding what is in his heart as the measure of repaying favor.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant does not assure himself that what he says must be correct, yet he holds that not hiding what is in his heart is the measure of repaying your grace.

sentences.zh: 若萬一足采，則微臣更生之年；

translations.literal: If by chance anything is worth adopting, then it will be a year of renewed life for this low minister;
translations.idiomatic: If by chance anything here is worth adopting, it will be as a year of renewed life for this lowly minister;

sentences.zh: 如皆瞽妄，則國之福也。

translations.literal: if all is blind and reckless, then it is the state's good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: if all is blind and reckless, then it is the state's good fortune.

sentences.zh: 願陛下缺半日之間，垂省臣言。

translations.literal: He wishes Your Majesty to set aside half a day and look down and examine your servant's words.
translations.idiomatic: He asks Your Majesty to set aside half a day and examine your servant's words.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下雖應天順人，龍飛踐阼，為創基之主，然所遇之時，實是叔世。

translations.literal: Prostrate, he considers that although Your Majesty responded to Heaven and accorded with men, soared as a dragon and ascended the throne, and is a lord who founded the base, yet the age he has encountered is in truth a declining generation.
translations.idiomatic: Prostrate, he considers that although Your Majesty responded to Heaven and accorded with men, soared as a dragon, and ascended the throne as a founder of the dynasty, the age you have encountered is in truth a declining one.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 漢末陵遲，閹豎用事，小人專朝，君子在野，政荒眾散，遂以亂亡。

translations.literal: At the end of Han the realm declined; eunuchs held power, petty men monopolized the court, gentlemen remained in the wilds, government was wasteland and the multitude scattered, and so it perished in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han the realm declined; eunuchs held power, petty men monopolized the court, gentlemen remained in retirement, government fell into ruin and the people scattered, and so the dynasty perished in disorder.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝以經略之才，撥煩理亂，兼肅文教，積數十年，至於延康之初，然後吏清下順，法始大行。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei, with talent for strategy and planning, cleared away troubles and ordered disorder, and together made civil teaching solemn; accumulating several decades, by the beginning of Yankang, only then were officials clear and the lower ranks compliant, and the law first broadly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei, with talent for strategy and planning, cleared away troubles and ordered disorder while also making civil teaching solemn; after several decades, by the beginning of the Yankang era, officials were finally upright, the lower ranks compliant, and the law broadly enforced.

sentences.zh: 逮至文、明二帝，奢淫驕縱，傾殆之主也。

translations.literal: Reaching the two emperors Wen and Ming, they were extravagant, dissolute, proud, and unrestrained—rulers who tilted toward peril.
translations.idiomatic: By the reigns of Emperors Wen and Ming, the throne was held by rulers who were extravagant, dissolute, proud, and unrestrained—sovereigns who tilted the dynasty toward peril.

sentences.zh: 然內盛台榭聲色之娛，外當三方英豪嚴敵，事成克舉，少有愆違，其故何也？

translations.literal: Yet within they flourished in towers, terraces, and the pleasures of sound and color; without they faced heroic foes on three sides and stern enemies—affairs succeeded and were accomplished, with little fault or failure; what was the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Yet within they flourished in towers, terraces, and the pleasures of sound and color; without they faced heroic foes on three sides and stern enemies—affairs succeeded and were accomplished with little fault or failure; what was the reason?

sentences.zh: 實賴前緒，以濟勳業。

translations.literal: In truth they relied on what had gone before to complete their achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In truth they relied on what had gone before to complete their achievement.

sentences.zh: 然法物政刑，固已漸穨矣。

translations.literal: Yet the ritual objects, government, and punishments had already gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ritual objects, government, and punishments had already gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 自嘉平之初，晉祚始基，逮於咸熙之末，其間累年。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Jiaping the Jin fortune first laid its foundation; reaching the end of Xianxi, many years lay between.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning of Jiaping the Jin dynasty first laid its foundation; by the end of Xianxi many years had passed.

sentences.zh: 雖鈇鉞屢斷，翦除凶醜，然其存者咸蒙遭時之恩，不軌於法。

translations.literal: Although axes and halberds were repeatedly applied and fierce villains were cut down and removed, yet those who remained all received the grace of the age and went outside the track of law.
translations.idiomatic: Although axes and halberds were repeatedly applied and fierce villains were cut down, those who remained all received the grace of the age and went outside the track of law.

sentences.zh: 泰始之初，陛下踐阼，其所服乘皆先代功臣之胤，非其子孫，則其曾玄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi Your Majesty ascended the throne; those who served and attended him were all descendants of meritorious ministers of former generations—if not their sons and grandsons, then their great-great-grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi Your Majesty ascended the throne; those who served and attended you were all descendants of meritorious ministers of former generations—if not their sons and grandsons, then their great-great-grandsons.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，膏粱之性難正，故曰時遇叔世。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: the nature of the rich and noble is hard to correct; hence it is said that the age encountered is a declining one.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that the nature of the rich and noble is hard to correct; hence it is said that the age you encountered is a declining one.

sentences.zh: 當此之秋，天地之位始定，四海洗心整綱之會也。

translations.literal: In this season the positions of Heaven and Earth were first fixed—it was the moment for the four seas to wash their hearts and put right the bonds of rule.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment the positions of Heaven and Earth were first fixed—it was the moment for the four seas to wash their hearts and put right the bonds of rule.

sentences.zh: 然陛下猶以用才因宜，法寬有由，積之在素，異于漢、魏之先。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty still took employing talent according to circumstance and the law's leniency as having its reasons, accumulated over long custom, different from Han and Wei before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty still held that employing talent according to circumstance and the law's leniency had their reasons, accumulated over long custom, unlike Han and Wei before.

sentences.zh: 三祖崛起，易朝之為，未可一旦直繩禦下，誠時宜也。

translations.literal: The Three Ancestors rose up and changed dynasties; one could not at once apply the straight cord to rule those below—it was truly suited to the time.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Ancestors rose up and changed dynasties; one could not at once apply the straight cord to rule those below—it was truly suited to the time.

sentences.zh: 然至所以為政，矯世眾務，自宜漸出公塗，法正威斷，日遷就肅。

translations.literal: Yet as to how one governs, correcting the age's many affairs, one should naturally gradually emerge onto the public path, make law upright and authority decisive, and day by day move toward severity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in governing and correcting the age's many affairs, one should naturally gradually emerge onto the public path, make law upright and authority decisive, and day by day move toward severity.

sentences.zh: 譬由行舟，雖不橫截迅流，然俄向所趣，漸靡而往，終得其濟。

translations.literal: It is like traveling by boat: although one does not cut straight across the swift current, yet in a little while, toward where one aims, one gradually drifts and goes, and in the end achieves crossing.
translations.idiomatic: It is like traveling by boat: although one does not cut straight across the swift current, one gradually drifts toward one's aim and in the end achieves the crossing.

sentences.zh: 積微稍著，以至於今，可以言政。

translations.literal: Accumulating the slight until it gradually appears, reaching to today, one may speak of government.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulating small changes until they gradually appear, reaching to the present, one may speak of government.

sentences.zh: 而自泰始以來，將三十年，政功美績，未稱聖旨，凡諸事業，不茂既往。

translations.literal: Yet from Taishi until now, nearly thirty years, governmental achievement and beautiful merit have not matched the sage intent; all various undertakings have not flourished beyond what went before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Taishi until now, nearly thirty years, governmental achievement and splendid merit have not matched your sage intent; none of the various undertakings has flourished beyond what went before.

sentences.zh: 以陛下明聖，猶未及叔世之弊，以成始初之隆，傳之後世，不無慮乎！

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's clarity and sagacity, still not reaching beyond the ills of a declining age to achieve the splendor of the beginning, transmitting it to later generations—is there not cause for concern!
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's clarity and sagacity, still not reaching beyond the ills of a declining age to achieve the splendor of the beginning and transmit it to later generations—is there not cause for concern!

sentences.zh: 意者，臣言豈不少概聖心夫！

translations.literal: Perhaps your servant's words do not a little touch the sage heart!
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps your servant's words do not a little touch Your Majesty's heart!

sentences.zh: 顧惟萬載之事，理在二端。

translations.literal: Looking to affairs of ten thousand generations, the principle lies in two points.
translations.idiomatic: Looking to affairs of ten thousand generations, the principle lies in two points.

sentences.zh: 天下大器，一安難傾，一傾難正。

translations.literal: The realm is a great vessel: once secure it is hard to overturn; once overturned it is hard to set right.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is a great vessel: once secure it is hard to overturn; once overturned it is hard to set right.

sentences.zh: 故慮經後世者，必精目下之政，政安遺業，使數世賴之。

translations.literal: Therefore one who considers and passes through later generations must refine the government of the present eye; when government secures the legacy, several generations may rely on it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one who plans for later generations must refine the government of the present; when government secures the legacy, several generations may rely on it.

sentences.zh: 若乃兼建諸侯而樹籓屏，深根固蒂，則祚延無窮，可以比跡三代。

translations.literal: If one moreover jointly establishes feudal lords and plants frontier screens, with deep roots and firm stems, then the fortune will extend without end and one may compare traces with the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: If one moreover jointly establishes feudal lords and plants frontier screens, with deep roots and firm stems, then the fortune will extend without end and one may compare traces with the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 如或當身之政，遺風餘烈不及後嗣，雖樹親戚，而成國之制不建，使夫後世獨任智力以安大業。

translations.literal: If the government of one's own person, with surviving wind and remaining vigor, does not reach later generations, although one plants kinsmen, yet the system of established states is not built, making later generations rely solely on intelligence and force to secure the great enterprise—
translations.idiomatic: If the government of one's own reign, with surviving influence and remaining vigor, does not reach later generations, then although kinsmen are planted, the system of established states is not built, and later generations must rely solely on intelligence and force to secure the great enterprise—

sentences.zh: 若未盡其理，雖經異時，憂責猶追在陛下，將如之何！

translations.literal: if one has not exhausted its principle, although time passes differently, worry and blame will still pursue Your Majesty—what then is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: if its principle is not fully realized, then although time passes, worry and blame will still pursue Your Majesty—what then is to be done!

sentences.zh: 願陛下善當今之政，樹不拔之勢，則天下無遺憂矣。

translations.literal: He wishes Your Majesty to manage well the government of today and plant an unuprootable power—then the realm will have no lingering worry.
translations.idiomatic: He asks Your Majesty to manage well the government of today and plant an unuprootable power—then the realm will have no lingering worry.

sentences.zh: 夫聖明不世及，後嗣不必賢，此天理之常也。

translations.literal: Sagely clarity does not come generation after generation, and later successors need not be worthy—this is the constant of Heaven's principle.
translations.idiomatic: Sagely clarity does not come generation after generation, and later successors need not be worthy—this is the constant way of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 故善為天下者，任勢而不任人。

translations.literal: Therefore one who is good at governing the realm relies on power and not on men.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one who is good at governing the realm relies on power and not on men.

sentences.zh: 任勢者，諸侯是也；

translations.literal: Those who rely on power are the feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: Those who rely on power are the feudal lords;

sentences.zh: 任人者，郡縣是也。

translations.literal: those who rely on men are the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: those who rely on men are the commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 郡縣之察，小政理而大勢危；

translations.literal: In the clarity of commanderies and counties, small government is well ordered but the great power is perilous;
translations.idiomatic: Under the clarity of commanderies and counties, small government is well ordered but the great power is perilous;

sentences.zh: 諸侯為邦，近多違而遠慮固。

translations.literal: when feudal lords govern states, near at hand there are many transgressions but far-sighted consideration is firm.
translations.idiomatic: when feudal lords govern states, near at hand there are many transgressions but far-sighted consideration is firm.

sentences.zh: 聖王推終始之弊，，權輕重之理，包彼小違以據大安，然後足以籓固內外，維鎮九服。

translations.literal: The sage king weighs the ills of beginning and end,, balances the principle of light and heavy, embraces those small transgressions to hold the great security, and only then is sufficient to screen and secure inner and outer and maintain the nine domains.
translations.idiomatic: The sage king weighs the ills of beginning and end, balances the principle of light and heavy, embraces those small transgressions to hold the great security, and only then is able to screen and secure inner and outer and maintain the nine domains.

sentences.zh: 夫武王聖主也，成王賢嗣也，然武王不恃成王之賢而廣封建者，慮經無窮也。

translations.literal: King Wu was a sage ruler and King Cheng a worthy successor; yet King Wu did not rely on King Cheng's worthiness and broadly enfeoffed because he considered and passed through without end.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu was a sage ruler and King Cheng a worthy successor; yet King Wu did not rely on King Cheng's worthiness and broadly enfeoffed because he planned for endless generations.

sentences.zh: 且善言今者，必有驗之于古。

translations.literal: Moreover, one who speaks well of the present must have verification in the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, one who speaks well of the present must have verification in the ancients.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞以前，書文殘缺，其事難詳。

translations.literal: Before Tang and Yu, written texts were broken and missing; those affairs are hard to detail.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tang and Yu, written texts were broken and missing; those affairs are hard to detail.

sentences.zh: 至於三代，則並建明德，及興王之顯親，列爵五等，開國承家，以籓屏帝室，延祚久長，近者五六百歲，遠者僅將千載。

translations.literal: Reaching the Three Dynasties, they jointly established the bright and virtuous, and the illustrious kin of founding kings; they ranked the five ranks of nobility, opened states and continued houses, to screen the imperial house; their fortune extended long—near at hand five or six hundred years, far off nearly a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the Three Dynasties, they jointly established the bright and virtuous and the illustrious kin of founding kings; they ranked the five ranks of nobility, opened states and continued houses to screen the imperial house; their fortune extended long—near at hand five or six hundred years, far off nearly a thousand.

sentences.zh: 逮至秦氏，罷侯置守，子弟不分尺土，孤立無輔，二世而亡。

translations.literal: Reaching the Qin house, they abolished marquises and set up governors; sons and younger brothers were not allotted even a foot of land; isolated without support, they perished in the second generation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qin house came, they abolished marquises and set up governors; sons and younger brothers were not allotted even a foot of land; isolated without support, they perished in the second generation.

sentences.zh: 漢承周、秦之後，雜而用之，前後二代各二百餘年。

translations.literal: Han succeeded after Zhou and Qin and used both mixed together; the two generations before and after each lasted more than two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Han succeeded Zhou and Qin and used both systems mixed together; the two periods before and after each lasted more than two hundred years.

sentences.zh: 揆其封建不用，雖強弱不適，制度舛錯，不盡事中，然跡其衰亡，恆在同姓失職，諸侯微時，不在強盛。

translations.literal: Measuring that enfeoffment was not used, although strong and weak were ill matched and institutions were awry and not fully suited to affairs, yet tracing their decline and fall, it was constantly when those of the same surname lost office and feudal lords were weak in their time—not when they were strong and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring that enfeoffment was not used, although strong and weak were ill matched and institutions were awry and not fully suited to affairs, yet tracing their decline and fall, it was constantly when those of the same surname lost office and feudal lords were weak in their time—not when they were strong and flourishing.

sentences.zh: 昔呂氏作亂，幸賴齊、代之援，以寧社稷。

translations.literal: Formerly when the Lü clan rebelled, they luckily relied on the aid of Qi and Dai to settle the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when the Lü clan rebelled, the realm luckily relied on the aid of Qi and Dai to settle the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 七國叛逆，梁王捍之，卒弭其難。

translations.literal: When the seven states rebelled, the King of Liang defended against them and in the end quelled the difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: When the seven states rebelled, the King of Liang defended against them and in the end quelled the crisis.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，威權削奪，諸侯止食租奉，甚者至乘牛車。

translations.literal: From this afterward, authority and power were cut and seized; feudal lords only ate rent and stipends, and in extreme cases even rode ox carts.
translations.idiomatic: From this afterward, authority and power were cut and seized; feudal lords only lived on rent and stipends, and in extreme cases even rode ox carts.

sentences.zh: 是以王莽得擅本朝，遂其奸謀，傾蕩天下，毒流生靈。

translations.literal: Therefore Wang Mang was able to monopolize the native court, carry out his treacherous plot, overturn and shake the realm, and spread poison among the living.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Wang Mang was able to monopolize the court, carry out his treacherous plot, overturn and shake the realm, and spread poison among the living.

sentences.zh: 光武紹起，雖封樹子弟，而不建成國之制，祚亦不延。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu rose up in succession; although he enfeoffed and planted sons and younger brothers, he did not establish the system of founded states, and the fortune also did not extend.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu rose up in succession; although he enfeoffed sons and younger brothers, he did not establish the system of founded states, and the fortune also did not extend.

sentences.zh: 魏氏承之，圈閉親戚，幽囚子弟，是以神器速傾，天命移在陛下。

translations.literal: The Wei house inherited this, penning in kinsmen and imprisoning sons and younger brothers; therefore the sacred vessel quickly tilted and Heaven's mandate shifted to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei house inherited this, penning in kinsmen and imprisoning sons and younger brothers; therefore the sacred vessel quickly tilted and Heaven's mandate shifted to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 長短之應，禍福之徵，可見於此。

translations.literal: The response of long and short, the sign of disaster and blessing, may be seen in this.
translations.idiomatic: The response of long and short reigns, the sign of disaster and blessing, may be seen in this.

sentences.zh: 又魏氏雖正位居體，南面稱帝，然三方未賓，正朔有所不加，實有戰國相持之勢。

translations.literal: Again, although the Wei house rightly occupied the position and body and faced south calling itself emperor, yet the three regions were not submitted and the calendar was not applied in some places; in truth there was the posture of the Warring States standing against one another.
translations.idiomatic: Again, although the Wei house rightly occupied the throne and faced south as emperor, the three regions were not submitted and the calendar was not applied everywhere; in truth there was the posture of the Warring States standing against one another.

sentences.zh: 大晉之興，宣帝定燕，太祖平蜀，陛下滅吳，可謂功格天地，土廣三王，舟車所至，人跡所及，皆為臣妾，四海大同，始於今日。

translations.literal: The rise of Great Jin: Emperor Xuan settled Yan, Emperor Taizu pacified Shu, Your Majesty destroyed Wu—it may be said that merit reached Heaven and Earth, territory broadened beyond the Three Kings; wherever boats and chariots reached, wherever human tracks extended, all became subjects; the four seas in great unity begins from today.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of Great Jin: Emperor Xuan settled Yan, Emperor Taizu pacified Shu, Your Majesty destroyed Wu—merit reaching Heaven and Earth, territory broadened beyond the Three Kings; wherever boats and chariots reached, wherever human tracks extended, all became subjects; the great unity of the four seas begins from today.

sentences.zh: 宜承大勳之籍，及陛下聖明之時，開啟土宇，使同姓必王，建久安于萬載，垂長世於無窮。

translations.literal: One should inherit the record of great achievement and, in Your Majesty's sage and bright time, open the realm, make those of the same surname necessarily kings, establish long peace for ten thousand generations, and extend long ages without end.
translations.idiomatic: One should inherit the record of great achievement and, in Your Majesty's sage and bright time, open the realm, make those of the same surname necessarily kings, establish long peace for ten thousand generations, and extend long ages without end.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞國有任臣則安，有重臣則亂。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that when a state has entrusted ministers it is secure, and when it has heavy ministers it is disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also heard that when a state has entrusted ministers it is secure, and when it has heavy ministers it is disordered.

sentences.zh: 而王制，人君立子以嫡不以長，立嫡以長不以賢，此事情之不可易者也。

translations.literal: Yet in royal institutions, the ruler establishes a son by legitimacy of birth and not by seniority, and establishes the legitimate heir by seniority and not by worth—this is what in affairs cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in royal institutions, the ruler establishes a son by legitimacy of birth and not by seniority, and establishes the legitimate heir by seniority and not by worth—this is what in affairs cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 而賢明至少，不肖至眾，此固天理之常也。

translations.literal: Yet the worthy and bright are at least few and the unworthy are at most many—this is indeed the constant of Heaven's principle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the worthy and bright are at best few and the unworthy are at most many—this is indeed the constant way of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 物類相求，感應而至，又自然也。

translations.literal: Things of a kind seek one another; responding and touching they arrive—this too is natural.
translations.idiomatic: Things of a kind seek one another; responding and touching they arrive—this too is natural.

sentences.zh: 是以暗君在位，則重臣盈朝；

translations.literal: Therefore when a dark ruler is on the throne, heavy ministers fill the court;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when a dark ruler is on the throne, heavy ministers fill the court;

sentences.zh: 明後臨政，則任臣列職。

translations.literal: when a bright sovereign governs, entrusted ministers fill the offices.
translations.idiomatic: when a bright sovereign governs, entrusted ministers fill the offices.

sentences.zh: 夫任臣之與重臣，俱執國統而立斷者也。

translations.literal: Entrusted ministers and heavy ministers alike hold the state's succession and establish decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted ministers and heavy ministers alike hold the state's succession and establish decisions.

sentences.zh: 然成敗相反，邪正相背，其故何也？

translations.literal: Yet success and failure are opposite, the crooked and straight turn their backs—what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Yet success and failure are opposite, the crooked and straight turn their backs—what is the reason?

sentences.zh: 重臣假所資以樹私，任臣因所籍以盡公。

translations.literal: Heavy ministers borrow what they rely on to plant private interest; entrusted ministers by what they rest upon exhaust the public good.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy ministers borrow what they rely on to plant private interest; entrusted ministers by what they rest upon exhaust the public good.

sentences.zh: 盡公者，政之本也；

translations.literal: Exhausting the public good is the root of government;
translations.idiomatic: Exhausting the public good is the root of government;

sentences.zh: 樹私者，亂之源也。

translations.literal: planting private interest is the source of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: planting private interest is the source of disorder.

sentences.zh: 推斯言之，則泰日少，亂日多，政教漸穨，欲國之無危，不可得也。

translations.literal: Extending this saying, then peaceful days are few and disorderly days many; government and teaching gradually decline—wishing the state to be without peril is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Extending this saying, peaceful days are few and disorderly days many; government and teaching gradually decline—wishing the state to be without peril is impossible.

sentences.zh: 又非徒唯然而已。

translations.literal: And this is not merely so and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: And this is not merely so and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 借令愚劣之嗣，蒙先哲之遺緒，得中賢之佐，而樹國本根不深，無干輔之固，則所謂任臣者化而為重臣矣。

translations.literal: Suppose a foolish and inferior successor, receiving the remnant threads of former sages and obtaining assistants of middling worth, yet the planted state's roots are not deep and there is no firmness of supporting trunks—then the so-called entrusted ministers transform into heavy ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose a foolish and inferior successor, receiving the remnant threads of former sages and obtaining assistants of middling worth, yet the planted state's roots are not deep and there is no firmness of supporting trunks—then the so-called entrusted ministers transform into heavy ministers.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 國有可傾之勢，則執權者見疑，眾疑難以自信，而甘受死亡者非人情故也。

translations.literal: When the state has a posture that may be overturned, then those who hold power are viewed with suspicion; when the multitude is suspicious it is hard to trust oneself, and willingly accepting death is not human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: When the state has a posture that may be overturned, those who hold power are viewed with suspicion; when the multitude is suspicious it is hard to trust oneself, and willingly accepting death is not human nature.

sentences.zh: 若乃建基既厚，籓屏強禦，雖置幼君赤子而天下不懼，曩之所謂重臣者，今悉反忠而為任臣矣。

translations.literal: If the foundation is already thick and the frontier screens strong in defense, then even if an infant ruler or suckling child is set up the realm is not afraid; the so-called heavy ministers of former times now all turn loyal and become entrusted ministers.
translations.idiomatic: If the foundation is already thick and the frontier screens strong in defense, then even if an infant ruler or suckling child is set up the realm is not afraid; the so-called heavy ministers of former times now all turn loyal and become entrusted ministers.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 理無危勢，懷不自猜，忠誠得著，不惕於邪故也。

translations.literal: Principle has no perilous posture; in the heart one does not suspect oneself; loyalty and sincerity obtain display; one is not wary of the crooked.
translations.idiomatic: Principle has no perilous posture; in the heart one does not suspect oneself; loyalty and sincerity obtain display; one is not wary of the crooked.

sentences.zh: 聖王知賢哲之不世及，故立相持之勢以禦其臣。

translations.literal: The sage king knows that the worthy and wise do not come generation after generation; therefore he establishes a mutually sustaining posture to guard against his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The sage king knows that the worthy and wise do not come generation after generation; therefore he establishes a mutually sustaining posture to guard against his ministers.

sentences.zh: 是以五等既列，臣無忠慢，同於竭節，以徇其上。

translations.literal: Therefore once the five ranks are arrayed, ministers have no loyal sloth; they are the same in exhausting integrity to follow their superior.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore once the five ranks are arrayed, ministers have no loyal sloth; they are the same in exhausting integrity to follow their superior.

sentences.zh: 群後既建，繼體賢鄙，亦均一契，等於無慮。

translations.literal: Once the host of lords is established, successors worthy or base are also equal in one tally, equal to being without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Once the host of lords is established, successors worthy or base are also equal in one tally, equal to being without worry.

sentences.zh: 且樹國苟固，則所任之臣，得賢益理，次委中智，亦足以安。

translations.literal: Moreover, if the planted state is firm, then the ministers entrusted—if the worthy are obtained, government is further ordered; if next entrusted to middling intelligence, that too is sufficient for security.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if the planted state is firm, then the ministers entrusted—if the worthy are obtained, government is further ordered; if next entrusted to middling intelligence, that too is sufficient for security.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 勢固易持故也。

translations.literal: Power firm is easy to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Power once firm is easy to hold.

sentences.zh: 然則建邦苟盡其理，則無向不可。

translations.literal: Thus if establishing states exhausts its principle, then there is no direction in which one may not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus if establishing states exhausts its principle, then there is no direction in which one may not succeed.

sentences.zh: 是以周室自成、康以下，逮至宣王，宣王之後，到于赧王，其間曆載，朝無名臣，而宗廟不隕者，諸侯維持之也。

translations.literal: Therefore from King Cheng and King Kang downward in the Zhou house, reaching King Xuan, and after King Xuan down to King Nan, years passed between; the court had no famous ministers yet the ancestral temple did not fall—feudal lords maintained it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore from Kings Cheng and Kang downward in the Zhou house, reaching King Xuan, and after King Xuan down to King Nan, years passed between; the court had no famous ministers yet the ancestral temple did not fall—feudal lords maintained it.

sentences.zh: 故曰，為社稷計，莫若建國。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said that in calculating for the altars of soil and grain, nothing is like establishing states.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said that in calculating for the altars of soil and grain, nothing is like establishing states.

sentences.zh: 夫邪正逆順者，人心之所系服也。

translations.literal: The crooked and straight, the rebellious and compliant—these are what men's hearts attach to and submit to.
translations.idiomatic: The crooked and straight, the rebellious and compliant—these are what men's hearts attach to and submit to.

sentences.zh: 今之建置，宜審量事勢，使諸侯率義而動，同忿俱奮，令其力足以維帶京邑。

translations.literal: In today's establishment, one should carefully measure affairs and power, making feudal lords lead righteousness in action, share anger and together exert themselves, so that their strength is sufficient to bind and gird the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In today's establishment, one should carefully measure affairs and power, making feudal lords lead righteousness in action, share anger and together exert themselves, so that their strength is sufficient to bind and gird the capital region.

sentences.zh: 若包藏禍心，惕於邪而起，孤立無党，所蒙之籍不足獨以有為。

translations.literal: If one harbors a treacherous heart, is wary and rises from the crooked, isolated without faction, the registers one receives are not sufficient to act alone.
translations.idiomatic: If one harbors a treacherous heart, is wary and rises from the crooked, isolated without faction, the registers one receives are not sufficient to act alone.

sentences.zh: 然齊此甚難，陛下宜與達古今善識事勢之士深共籌之。

translations.literal: Yet to align this is very difficult; Your Majesty should deeply consult together with men who penetrate antiquity and the present and are good at knowing affairs and power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to align this is very difficult; Your Majesty should deeply consult together with men who penetrate antiquity and the present and are good at knowing affairs and power.

sentences.zh: 建侯之理，使君樂其國，臣榮其朝，各流福祚，傳之無窮。

translations.literal: The principle of establishing marquises is to make lords delight in their states and ministers honor their court, each flowing fortune and blessing, transmitting them without end.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of establishing marquises is to make lords delight in their states and ministers honor their court, each flowing fortune and blessing, transmitting them without end.

sentences.zh: 上下一心，愛國如家，視百姓如子，然後能保荷天祿，兼翼王室。

translations.literal: Above and below of one heart, loving the state as home, viewing the hundred surnames as children—only then can one preserve and bear Heaven's blessing and together wing the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Above and below of one heart, loving the state as home, viewing the common people as children—only then can one preserve and bear Heaven's blessing and together wing the royal house.

sentences.zh: 今諸王裂土，皆兼于古之諸侯，而君賤其爵，臣恥其位，莫有安志，其故何也？

translations.literal: Now the various princes divide land, all combining the ancient feudal lords, yet lords despise their ranks and ministers are ashamed of their positions; none have a settled will—what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Now the various princes divide land, all combining the ancient feudal lords, yet lords despise their ranks and ministers are ashamed of their positions; none have a settled will—what is the reason?

sentences.zh: 法同郡縣，無成國之制故也。

translations.literal: The law is the same as commanderies and counties; there is no system of established states.
translations.idiomatic: The law is the same as commanderies and counties; there is no system of established states.

sentences.zh: 今之建置，宜使率由舊章，一如古典。

translations.literal: In today's establishment, one should make all follow the old statutes, exactly like the ancient model.
translations.idiomatic: In today's establishment, one should make all follow the old statutes, exactly like the ancient model.

sentences.zh: 然人心系常，不累十年，好惡未改，情願未移。

translations.literal: Yet men's hearts are tied to custom; within not ten years, likes and dislikes are not changed and inclinations are not shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men's hearts are tied to custom; within not ten years, likes and dislikes are not changed and inclinations are not shifted.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚慮，以為宜早創大制，遲回眾望，猶在十年之外，然後能令君臣各安其位，榮其所蒙，上下相持，用成籓輔。

translations.literal: In your servant's foolish thought, one should early create the great system; if one delays and turns back the multitude's hope, it will still be beyond ten years before one can make lord and minister each rest secure in his position, honor what he receives, above and below mutually sustain, and thereby complete frontier assistance.
translations.idiomatic: In your servant's humble view, one should early create the great system; if one delays and turns back the multitude's hope, it will still be beyond ten years before lord and minister can each rest secure in his position, honor what he receives, above and below mutually sustain, and thereby complete frontier assistance.

sentences.zh: 如今之為，適足以虧天府之藏，徒棄穀帛之資，無補鎮國衛上之勢也。

translations.literal: As it is done now, it is just sufficient to diminish the storehouse of Heaven's treasury, vainly discard resources of grain and cloth, and give no help to the power of stabilizing the state and guarding the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: As it is done now, it is just sufficient to diminish the storehouse of Heaven's treasury, vainly discard resources of grain and cloth, and give no help to the power of stabilizing the state and guarding the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 古者封建既定，各有其國，後雖王之子孫，無復尺土，此今事之必不行者也。

translations.literal: In antiquity, once enfeoffment was settled, each had his state; afterward, even the king's sons and grandsons had no more foot of land—this is what in present affairs certainly cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, once enfeoffment was settled, each had his state; afterward, even the king's sons and grandsons had no more foot of land—this is what in present affairs certainly cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 若推親疏，轉有所廢，以有所樹，則是郡縣之職，非建國之制。

translations.literal: If one pushes near and far kin, in turn abolishing here and planting there, then this is the duty of commanderies and counties, not the system of establishing states.
translations.idiomatic: If one pushes near and far kin, in turn abolishing here and planting there, then this is the duty of commanderies and counties, not the system of establishing states.

sentences.zh: 今宜豫開此地，令十世之內，使親者得轉處近。

translations.literal: Now one should beforehand open this ground, so that within ten generations those who are near kin may in turn be placed nearer.
translations.idiomatic: Now one should beforehand open this ground, so that within ten generations those who are near kin may in turn be placed nearer.

sentences.zh: 十世之遠，近郊地盡，然後親疏相維，不得復如十世之內。

translations.literal: At ten generations' distance, when the near suburban lands are exhausted, then near and far kin will mutually sustain one another and cannot again be as within ten generations.
translations.idiomatic: At ten generations' distance, when the near suburban lands are exhausted, then near and far kin will mutually sustain one another and cannot again be as within ten generations.

sentences.zh: 然猶樹親有所，遲天下都滿，已彌數百千年矣。

translations.literal: Yet still in planting kin there is a place; delaying until the realm is full has already spanned several hundred or thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet still in planting kin there is a place; delaying until the realm is full has already spanned several hundred or thousand years.

sentences.zh: 今方始封而親疏倒施，甚非所宜。

translations.literal: Now one has just begun to enfeoff yet near and far kin are reversed in application—this is very unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: Now one has just begun to enfeoff yet near and far kin are reversed in application—this is very unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 宜更大量天下土田方里之數，都更裂土分人，以王同姓，使親疏遠近不錯其宜，然後可以永安。

translations.literal: One should again greatly measure the numbers of land and square li throughout the realm, all again split land and divide people, making kings of the same surname, so that near and far kin, distant and close, do not miss their proper place—only then can there be lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: One should again greatly measure the numbers of land and square li throughout the realm, all again split land and divide people, making kings of the same surname, so that near and far kin, distant and close, do not miss their proper place—only then can there be lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 古者封國，大者不過土方百里，然後人數殷眾，境內必盈其力，足以備充制度。

translations.literal: In antiquity enfeoffed states, the largest did not exceed a hundred li square of land; then the population was abundant and numerous, and within the borders they necessarily filled their strength, sufficient to prepare and complete the institutions.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity enfeoffed states, the largest did not exceed a hundred li square of land; then the population was abundant and numerous, and within the borders they necessarily filled their strength, sufficient to prepare and complete the institutions.

sentences.zh: 今雖一國周環近將千里，然力實寡，不足以奉國典。

translations.literal: Now although one state circles nearly a thousand li, in truth its strength is sparse and insufficient to support the state's canon.
translations.idiomatic: Now although one state circles nearly a thousand li, in truth its strength is sparse and insufficient to support the state's canon.

sentences.zh: 所遇不同，故當因時制宜，以盡事適今。

translations.literal: What is encountered is different; therefore one should adapt institutions to the time, to exhaust affairs and suit the present.
translations.idiomatic: What is encountered is different; therefore one should adapt institutions to the time, to exhaust affairs and suit the present.

sentences.zh: 宜令諸王國容少而軍容多，然于古典所應有者悉立其制，然非急所須，漸而備之，不得頓設也。

translations.literal: One should order the various princes' state regalia to be few and military regalia many; yet among what the ancient model should have, fully establish its institutions; yet what is not urgently needed should gradually be prepared and must not be set up at once.
translations.idiomatic: One should order the various princes' state regalia to be few and military regalia many; yet among what the ancient model should have, fully establish its institutions; yet what is not urgently needed should gradually be prepared and must not be set up at once.

sentences.zh: 須車甲器械既具，群臣乃服彩章；

translations.literal: Only when chariots, armor, and weapons are complete do the host of ministers then wear colored insignia;
translations.idiomatic: Only when chariots, armor, and weapons are complete do the host of ministers then wear colored insignia;

sentences.zh: 倉廩已實，乃營宮室；

translations.literal: when granaries are already filled, then one builds palaces and halls;
translations.idiomatic: when granaries are already filled, then one builds palaces and halls;

sentences.zh: 百姓已足，乃備官司；

translations.literal: when the hundred surnames are already sufficient, then one prepares official offices;
translations.idiomatic: when the common people are already sufficient, then one prepares official offices;

sentences.zh: 境內充實，乃作禮樂。

translations.literal: when within the borders is full and solid, then one makes rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: when within the borders is full and solid, then one makes rites and music.

sentences.zh: 唯宗廟社稷，則先建之。

translations.literal: Only the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain should be built first.
translations.idiomatic: Only the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain should be built first.

sentences.zh: 至於境內之政，官人用才，自非內史、國相命于天子，其餘眾職及死生之斷、穀帛資實、慶賞刑威、非封爵者，悉得專之。

translations.literal: As to government within the borders and appointing men by talent, except that the inner scribe and state chancellor are appointed by the Son of Heaven, all other numerous offices and decisions of life and death, resources of grain and cloth, rewards and punishments, honors and authority, and matters other than enfeoffment of rank—all may be exclusively decided.
translations.idiomatic: As to government within the borders and appointing men by talent, except that the inner scribe and state chancellor are appointed by the Son of Heaven, all other offices and decisions of life and death, resources of grain and cloth, rewards and punishments, honors and authority, and matters other than enfeoffment of rank—all may be exclusively decided.

sentences.zh: 今臣所舉二端，蓋事之大較，其所不載，應在二端之屬者，以此為率。

translations.literal: What your servant now presents in two points is broadly the great outline of affairs; what is not recorded but should belong to the category of the two points should take this as the measure.
translations.idiomatic: What your servant now presents in two points is broadly the great outline of affairs; what is not recorded but should belong to the category of the two points should take this as the measure.

sentences.zh: 今諸國本一郡之政耳，若備舊典，則官司以數，事所不須，而以虛制損實力。

translations.literal: Now the various states are in origin only the government of one commandery; if one prepares the old canon, then official offices multiply in number, affairs not needed, and with empty institutions one damages real strength.
translations.idiomatic: Now the various states are in origin only the government of one commandery; if one prepares the old canon, then official offices multiply in number for affairs not needed, and with empty institutions one damages real strength.

sentences.zh: 至於慶賞刑斷，所以衛下之權，不重則無以威眾人而衛上。

translations.literal: As to rewards and punishments and judicial decisions—these are the authority by which one guards those below; if not weighty, one has no means to awe the multitude and guard the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: As to rewards and punishments and judicial decisions—these are the authority by which one guards those below; if not weighty, one has no means to awe the multitude and guard the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 故臣之愚慮，欲令諸侯權具，國容少而軍容多，然亦終於必備今事為宜。

translations.literal: Therefore in your servant's foolish thought, he wishes to make feudal lords' authority complete, with state regalia few and military regalia many; yet in the end it must also be fully prepared—as present affairs require.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in your servant's humble view, he wishes to make feudal lords' authority complete, with state regalia few and military regalia many; yet in the end it must also be fully prepared—as present affairs require.

sentences.zh: 周之建侯，長享其國，與王者並，遠者僅將千載，近者猶數百年；

translations.literal: Zhou's establishment of marquises: they long enjoyed their states, standing alongside the king; far off nearly a thousand years, near at hand still several hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's establishment of marquises: they long enjoyed their states, standing alongside the king; far off nearly a thousand years, near at hand still several hundred;

sentences.zh: 漢之諸王，傳祚暨至曾玄。

translations.literal: Han's various kings transmitted fortune reaching even to great-great-grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Han's various kings transmitted fortune reaching even to great-great-grandsons.

sentences.zh: 人性不甚相遠，古今一揆，而短長甚違，其故何邪？

translations.literal: Human nature is not very far apart; ancient and modern are one measure—yet short and long greatly diverge; what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Human nature is not very far apart; ancient and modern are one measure—yet short and long greatly diverge; what is the reason?

sentences.zh: 立意本殊而制不同故也。

translations.literal: The intent established was fundamentally different and the institutions were not the same.
translations.idiomatic: The intent established was fundamentally different and the institutions were not the same.

sentences.zh: 周之封建，使國重於君，公侯之身輕於社稷，故無道之君不免誅放。

translations.literal: Zhou's enfeoffment made the state heavier than the lord and the bodies of dukes and marquises lighter than the altars of soil and grain; therefore unprincipled lords did not escape execution and banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's enfeoffment made the state heavier than the lord and the bodies of dukes and marquises lighter than the altars of soil and grain; therefore unprincipled lords did not escape execution and banishment.

sentences.zh: 敦興滅繼絕之義，故國祚不泯。

translations.literal: They honored the principle of raising what was destroyed and continuing what was broken off; therefore state fortune was not extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: They honored the principle of raising what was destroyed and continuing what was broken off; therefore state fortune was not extinguished.

sentences.zh: 不免誅放，則群後思懼；

translations.literal: Not escaping execution and banishment, then the host of lords thought and feared;
translations.idiomatic: Not escaping execution and banishment, then the host of lords thought and feared;

sentences.zh: 胤嗣必繼，是無亡國也。

translations.literal: heirs and successors necessarily continued—there was no perishing state.
translations.idiomatic: heirs and successors necessarily continued—there was no perishing state.

sentences.zh: 諸侯思懼，然後軌道，下無亡國，天子乘之，理勢自安，此周室所以長在也。

translations.literal: Feudal lords thought and feared, and then followed the track; below there were no perishing states; the Son of Heaven rode upon this—principle and power naturally secure; this is why the Zhou house long endured.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords thought and feared, and then followed the track; below there were no perishing states; the Son of Heaven rode upon this—principle and power naturally secure; this is why the Zhou house long endured.

sentences.zh: 漢之樹置君國，輕重不殊，故諸王失度，陷於罪戮，國隨以亡。

translations.literal: Han in planting and setting up lords and states made light and heavy not different; therefore various kings lost measure, fell into crime and punishment, and states followed in perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Han in planting and setting up lords and states made light and heavy not different; therefore various kings lost measure, fell into crime and punishment, and states followed in perishing.

sentences.zh: 不崇興滅繼絕之序，故下無固國。

translations.literal: They did not honor the order of raising what was destroyed and continuing what was broken off; therefore below there were no firm states.
translations.idiomatic: They did not honor the order of raising what was destroyed and continuing what was broken off; therefore below there were no firm states.

sentences.zh: 下無固國，天子居上，勢孤無輔，故奸臣擅朝，易傾大業。

translations.literal: Below there were no firm states; the Son of Heaven dwelt above, power isolated without assistance; therefore treacherous ministers monopolized the court and easily overturned the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Below there were no firm states; the Son of Heaven dwelt above, power isolated without assistance; therefore treacherous ministers monopolized the court and easily overturned the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 今宜反漢之弊，修周舊跡。

translations.literal: Now one should reverse Han's ills and repair Zhou's old traces.
translations.idiomatic: Now one should reverse Han's ills and repair Zhou's old traces.

sentences.zh: 國君雖或失道，陷於誅絕，又無子應除，苟有始封支胤，不問遠近，必紹其祚。

translations.literal: Although a state's lord may lose the Way and fall into execution and extinction, and again have no son who should be removed, if there is a branch descendant of the original enfeoffment, without asking near or far, he must continue its fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Although a state's lord may lose the Way and fall into execution and extinction, and again have no son who should succeed, if there is a branch descendant of the original enfeoffment, without asking near or far, he must continue its fortune.

sentences.zh: 若無遺類，則虛建之，須皇子生，以繼其統，然後建國無滅。

translations.literal: If there is no surviving line, then establish it in vacancy; when an imperial son is born, let him continue its succession—only then will established states not perish.
translations.idiomatic: If there is no surviving line, then establish it in vacancy; when an imperial son is born, let him continue its succession—only then will established states not perish.

sentences.zh: 又班固稱「諸侯失國亦猶網密」，今又宜都寬其檢。

translations.literal: Again Ban Gu said, "When feudal lords lose their states it is also like a net being tight"; now one should also broadly loosen their scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Again Ban Gu said, "When feudal lords lose their states it is also like a net being tight"; now one should also broadly loosen their scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 且建侯之理，本經盛衰，大制都定，班之群後，著誓丹青，書之玉版，藏之金匱，置諸宗廟，副在有司。

translations.literal: Moreover, the principle of establishing marquises fundamentally passes through flourishing and decline; once the great system is fully settled, distribute it to the host of lords, inscribe the oath in cinnabar, write it on jade tablets, store it in a golden coffer, place it in the ancestral temple, and keep a copy with the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the principle of establishing marquises fundamentally passes through flourishing and decline; once the great system is fully settled, distribute it to the host of lords, inscribe the oath in cinnabar, write it on jade tablets, store it in a golden coffer, place it in the ancestral temple, and keep a copy with the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 寡弱小國猶不可危，豈況萬乘之主！

translations.literal: Even a small state that is weak and few may not be endangered—how much more the lord of ten thousand chariots!
translations.idiomatic: Even a small state that is weak and few may not be endangered—how much more the lord of ten thousand chariots!

sentences.zh: 承難傾之邦而加其上，則自然永久居重固之安，可謂根深華嶽而四維之也。

translations.literal: Inheriting a state hard to overturn and placing it above, one naturally forever dwells in heavy and firm security—it may be said that roots are deep as Mount Hua and the four corners are bound.
translations.idiomatic: Inheriting a state hard to overturn and placing it above, one naturally forever dwells in heavy and firm security—it may be said that roots are deep as Mount Hua and the four corners are bound.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚，願陛下置天下于自安之地，寄大業于固成之勢，則可以無遺憂矣。

translations.literal: In your servant's foolishness, he wishes Your Majesty to place the realm in a place of self-security and entrust the great enterprise to a posture already firm and formed—then one may be without lingering worry.
translations.idiomatic: In your servant's humble view, he wishes Your Majesty to place the realm in a place of self-security and entrust the great enterprise to a posture already firm and formed—then one may be without lingering worry.

sentences.zh: 今閻閭少名士，官司無高能，其故何也？

translations.literal: Now in lanes and wards there are few famous scholars, and in official offices there are no men of high ability—what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Now in lanes and wards there are few famous scholars, and in official offices there are no men of high ability—what is the reason?

sentences.zh: 清議不肅，人不立德，行在取容，故無名士。

translations.literal: Pure discussion is not solemn; men do not establish virtue; conduct lies in gaining acceptance—therefore there are no famous scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Pure discussion is not solemn; men do not establish virtue; conduct lies in gaining acceptance—therefore there are no famous scholars.

sentences.zh: 下不專局，又無考課，吏不竭節，故無高能。

translations.literal: Below, offices are not specialized, and again there is no examination and assessment; clerks do not exhaust integrity—therefore there are no men of high ability.
translations.idiomatic: Below, offices are not specialized, and again there is no examination and assessment; clerks do not exhaust integrity—therefore there are no men of high ability.

sentences.zh: 無高能，則有疾世事；

translations.literal: Without men of high ability, there are those who resent worldly affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Without men of high ability, there are those who resent worldly affairs;

sentences.zh: 少名士，則後進無准，故臣思立吏課而肅清議。

translations.literal: with few famous scholars, those who come after have no standard; therefore your servant thinks to establish clerk assessment and make pure discussion solemn.
translations.idiomatic: with few famous scholars, those who come after have no standard; therefore your servant thinks to establish clerk assessment and make pure discussion solemn.

sentences.zh: 夫欲富貴而惡貧賤，人理然也。

translations.literal: To desire wealth and rank and hate poverty and baseness is human reason as it is.
translations.idiomatic: To desire wealth and rank and hate poverty and baseness is human nature.

sentences.zh: 聖王大諳物情，知不可去，故直同公私之利，而詭其求道，使夫欲富者必先由貧，欲貴者必先安賤。

translations.literal: The sage king greatly understands the feelings of things, knows they cannot be removed, and therefore directly makes public and private profit the same, yet artfully arranges the path of seeking, so that those who wish to be rich must first pass through poverty and those who wish to be noble must first rest content in baseness.
translations.idiomatic: The sage king greatly understands human feelings, knows they cannot be removed, and therefore directly makes public and private profit the same, yet artfully arranges the path of seeking, so that those who wish to be rich must first pass through poverty and those who wish to be noble must first rest content in baseness.

sentences.zh: 安賤則不矜，不矜然後廉恥厲；

translations.literal: Resting content in baseness, then one is not proud; not being proud, then integrity and shame are sharpened;
translations.idiomatic: Resting content in baseness, then one is not proud; not being proud, then integrity and shame are sharpened;

sentences.zh: 守貧者必節欲，節欲然後操全。

translations.literal: those who keep poverty necessarily restrain desire; restraining desire, then conduct is complete.
translations.idiomatic: those who keep poverty necessarily restrain desire; restraining desire, then conduct is complete.

sentences.zh: 以此處務，乃得盡公。

translations.literal: With this to handle affairs, one then obtains exhausting the public good.
translations.idiomatic: With this to handle affairs, one then obtains exhausting the public good.

sentences.zh: 盡公者，富貴之徒也。

translations.literal: Those who exhaust the public good are the company of wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Those who exhaust the public good are the company of wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 為無私者終得其私，故公私之利同也。

translations.literal: Those who act without private interest ultimately obtain their private interest; therefore public and private profit are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Those who act without private interest ultimately obtain their private interest; therefore public and private profit are the same.

sentences.zh: 今欲富者不由貧自得富，欲貴者不安賤自得貴，公私之塗既乖，而人情不能無私，私利不可以公得，則恆背公而橫務。

translations.literal: Now those who wish to be rich obtain riches without passing through poverty; those who wish to be noble obtain nobility without resting content in baseness; the paths of public and private are already at odds, yet human feeling cannot be without private interest; private profit cannot be obtained through the public—then one constantly turns from the public and recklessly pursues affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Now those who wish to be rich obtain riches without passing through poverty; those who wish to be noble obtain nobility without resting content in baseness; the paths of public and private are already at odds, yet human feeling cannot be without private interest; private profit cannot be obtained through the public—then one constantly turns from the public and recklessly pursues affairs.

sentences.zh: 是以風節日穨，公理漸替，人士富貴，非軌道之所得。

translations.literal: Therefore wind and integrity daily decline, public reason gradually fades, and scholars' wealth and rank are not what is obtained by following the track.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore integrity daily declines, public reason gradually fades, and scholars' wealth and rank are not what is obtained by following the track.

sentences.zh: 以此為政，小大難期。

translations.literal: Using this to govern, small and great are hard to expect.
translations.idiomatic: Using this to govern, small and great affairs are hard to expect.

sentences.zh: 然教穨來既久，難反一朝。
