translations.literal: Yet teaching has declined and come for long; it is hard to reverse in one morning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet teaching has declined for long; it is hard to reverse in one morning.

sentences.zh: 又世放都靡，營欲比肩，群士渾然，庸行相似，不可頓肅，甚殊黜陟也。

translations.literal: Again, the age is unrestrained and the capital dissolute; pursuing desire shoulder to shoulder, the host of scholars are all alike and vulgar conduct is similar—it cannot be suddenly made solemn, and promotion and demotion would be very disparate.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the age is unrestrained and the capital dissolute; pursuing desire shoulder to shoulder, the host of scholars are all alike and vulgar conduct is similar—it cannot be suddenly made solemn, and promotion and demotion would be very disparate.

sentences.zh: 且教不求盡善，善在抑尤，同侈之中，猶有甚泰。

translations.literal: Moreover, teaching does not seek complete goodness; goodness lies in restraining extremes; among the equally extravagant, there are still those very excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, teaching does not seek complete goodness; goodness lies in restraining extremes; among the equally extravagant, there are still those very excessive.

sentences.zh: 使夫昧適情之樂者，捐其顯榮之貴，俄在不鮮之地；

translations.literal: Make those who are blind to the pleasure of fitting feeling abandon their displayed glory and honor, and in a little while be in a place not fresh;
translations.idiomatic: Make those who are blind to the pleasure of fitting feeling abandon their displayed glory and honor, and in a little while be in a place not fresh;

sentences.zh: 約己潔素者，蒙儉德之報，列于清官之上。

translations.literal: those who restrain themselves and are pure and plain receive the reward of frugal virtue and are ranked above clear offices.
translations.idiomatic: those who restrain themselves and are pure and plain receive the reward of frugal virtue and are ranked above clear offices.

sentences.zh: 二業分流，令各有蒙。

translations.literal: The two pursuits divide into streams, making each have what he receives.
translations.idiomatic: The two pursuits divide into streams, making each have what he receives.

sentences.zh: 然俗放都奢，不可頓肅，故臣私慮，願先從事於漸也。

translations.literal: Yet custom is unrestrained and the capital extravagant; it cannot be suddenly made solemn; therefore in your servant's private thought he wishes first to engage in gradual progress.
translations.idiomatic: Yet custom is unrestrained and the capital extravagant; it cannot be suddenly made solemn; therefore in your servant's private thought he wishes first to engage in gradual progress.

sentences.zh: 天下至大，萬事至眾，人君至少，同于天日，故非垂聽所得周覽。

translations.literal: The realm is greatest, the myriad affairs most numerous, and the ruler is least—like Heaven and the sun; therefore it is not what listening downward can fully survey.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is greatest, the myriad affairs most numerous, and the ruler is least—like Heaven and the sun; therefore it is not what listening downward can fully survey.

sentences.zh: 是以聖王之化，執要而已，委務於下而不以事自嬰也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage king's transformation holds the essential and nothing more, entrusting affairs to those below and not binding himself with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage king's transformation holds the essential and nothing more, entrusting affairs to those below and not binding himself with affairs.

sentences.zh: 分職既定，無所與焉，非憚日昃之勤，而牽於逸豫之虞，誠以政體宜然，事勢致之也。

translations.literal: Once divided duties are settled, he has no part in them; it is not that he fears the diligence of the sun's setting, but that he is pulled by worry over ease and pleasure—in truth the body of government should be so; affairs and power bring it about.
translations.idiomatic: Once divided duties are settled, he has no part in them; it is not that he fears the diligence of the sun's setting, but that he is pulled by worry over ease and pleasure—in truth the body of government should be so; affairs and power bring it about.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 夫造創謀始，逆暗是非，以別能否，甚難察也。

translations.literal: Creating and planning the beginning, going against darkness to distinguish right and wrong and separate able from unable—is very hard to discern.
translations.idiomatic: Creating and planning the beginning, going against darkness to distinguish right and wrong and separate able from unable—is very hard to discern.

sentences.zh: 既以施行，因其成敗，以分功罪，甚易識也。

translations.literal: Once it has been implemented, following its success and failure to divide merit and guilt—is very easy to recognize.
translations.idiomatic: Once it has been implemented, following its success and failure to divide merit and guilt—is very easy to recognize.

sentences.zh: 易識在考終，難察在造始，故人君恆居其易則安，人臣不處其難則亂。

translations.literal: Easy to recognize lies in examining the end; hard to discern lies in creating the beginning; therefore the ruler constantly dwells in what is easy and is secure, while ministers do not occupy what is hard and there is disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Easy to recognize lies in examining the end; hard to discern lies in creating the beginning; therefore the ruler constantly dwells in what is easy and is secure, while ministers do not occupy what is hard and there is disorder.

sentences.zh: 今陛下每精事始而略於考終，故群吏慮事懷成敗之懼輕，飾文采以避目下之譴重，此政功所以未善也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty each time is precise at the beginning of affairs yet brief in examining the end; therefore the host of clerks, considering affairs, hold lightly the fear of success and failure and adorn literary color to avoid the heavy censure of the present eye—this is why governmental achievement is not yet good.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty each time is precise at the beginning of affairs yet brief in examining the end; therefore the host of clerks, considering affairs, hold lightly the fear of success and failure and adorn literary color to avoid the heavy censure of the present eye—this is why governmental achievement is not yet good.

sentences.zh: 今人主能恆居易執要以禦其下，然後人臣功罪形於成敗之征，無逃其誅賞。

translations.literal: Now if the ruler can constantly dwell in what is easy and hold the essential to guard against those below, then ministers' merit and guilt take form in the signs of success and failure and cannot escape punishment and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Now if the ruler can constantly dwell in what is easy and hold the essential to guard against those below, then ministers' merit and guilt take form in the signs of success and failure and cannot escape punishment and reward.

sentences.zh: 故罪不可蔽，功不可誣。

translations.literal: Therefore guilt cannot be hidden and merit cannot be falsely charged.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore guilt cannot be hidden and merit cannot be falsely charged.

sentences.zh: 功不可誣，則能者勸；

translations.literal: Merit cannot be falsely charged, then the able are encouraged;
translations.idiomatic: Merit cannot be falsely charged, then the able are encouraged;

sentences.zh: 罪不可蔽，則違慢日肅，此為國之大略也。

translations.literal: guilt cannot be hidden, then transgression and sloth daily grow solemn—this is the great outline of governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: guilt cannot be hidden, then transgression and sloth daily grow solemn—this is the great outline of governing the state.

sentences.zh: 臣竊惟陛下聖心，意在盡善，懼政有違，故精事始，以求無失。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers Your Majesty's sage heart: the intent lies in complete goodness, fearing that government may transgress; therefore he is precise at the beginning of affairs, seeking to be without failure.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately considers Your Majesty's sage heart: the intent lies in complete goodness, fearing that government may transgress; therefore you are precise at the beginning of affairs, seeking to be without failure.

sentences.zh: 又以眾官勝任者少，故不委務，甯居日昃也。

translations.literal: Again, because among the multitude of officials few are competent, he does not entrust affairs and would rather dwell at the sun's setting.
translations.idiomatic: Again, because among the multitude of officials few are competent, you do not entrust affairs and would rather dwell at the sun's setting.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚慮，竊以為今欲盡善，故宜考終。

translations.literal: In your servant's foolish thought, he privately holds that now wishing for complete goodness, one should therefore examine the end.
translations.idiomatic: In your servant's humble view, he privately holds that now wishing for complete goodness, one should therefore examine the end.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 精始難校故也。

translations.literal: Because being precise at the beginning is hard to verify.
translations.idiomatic: Because being precise at the beginning is hard to verify.

sentences.zh: 又群官多不勝任，亦宜委務，使能者得以成功，不能者得以著敗。

translations.literal: Again, many officials are not competent; one should also entrust affairs, so that the able may achieve success and the unable may show failure.
translations.idiomatic: Again, many officials are not competent; one should also entrust affairs, so that the able may achieve success and the unable may show failure.

sentences.zh: 敗著可得而廢，功成可得遂任，然後賢能常居位以善事，暗劣不得以屍祿害政。

translations.literal: Failure shown may be obtained and dismissed; success achieved may be obtained and continued in office; then the worthy and able constantly hold position to handle affairs well, and the dark and inferior may not by corpse stipend harm government.
translations.idiomatic: Failure shown may be obtained and dismissed; success achieved may be obtained and continued in office; then the worthy and able constantly hold position to handle affairs well, and the dark and inferior may not by corpse stipend harm government.

sentences.zh: 如此不已，則勝任者漸多，經年少久，即群司遍得其人矣。

translations.literal: If this continues without end, then the competent gradually increase; after years, little by little, then the host of offices everywhere obtain their men.
translations.idiomatic: If this continues without end, then the competent gradually increase; after years, little by little, the host of offices everywhere obtain their men.

sentences.zh: 此校才考實，政之至務也。

translations.literal: This comparing talent and examining reality is the utmost task of government.
translations.idiomatic: This comparing talent and examining reality is the utmost task of government.

sentences.zh: 今人主不委事仰成，而與諸下共造事始，則功罪難分。

translations.literal: Now when the ruler does not entrust affairs and look upward for completion, but together with those below creates the beginning of affairs, then merit and guilt are hard to divide.
translations.idiomatic: Now when the ruler does not entrust affairs and look upward for completion, but together with those below creates the beginning of affairs, then merit and guilt are hard to divide.

sentences.zh: 下不專事，居官不久，故能否不別。

translations.literal: Those below do not specialize in affairs and do not long hold office; therefore able and unable are not distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Those below do not specialize in affairs and do not long hold office; therefore able and unable are not distinguished.

sentences.zh: 何以驗之？

translations.literal: How may this be verified?
translations.idiomatic: How may this be verified?

sentences.zh: 今世士人決不悉良能也，又決不悉疲軟也。

translations.literal: In the present age scholars are certainly not all thoroughly able, and again are certainly not all thoroughly weak and soft.
translations.idiomatic: In the present age scholars are certainly not all thoroughly able, and again are certainly not all thoroughly weak and soft.

sentences.zh: 然今欲舉一忠賢，不知所賞；

translations.literal: Yet now wishing to promote one loyal and worthy, one does not know whom to reward;
translations.idiomatic: Yet now wishing to promote one loyal and worthy, one does not know whom to reward;

sentences.zh: 求一負敗，不知所罰。

translations.literal: seeking one who bears failure, one does not know whom to punish.
translations.idiomatic: seeking one who bears failure, one does not know whom to punish.

sentences.zh: 及其免退，自以犯法耳，非不能也。

translations.literal: When they are dismissed and retire, they themselves think it is because they violated law—not because they were unable.
translations.idiomatic: When they are dismissed and retire, they themselves think it is because they violated law—not because they were unable.

sentences.zh: 登進者自以累資及人間之譽耳，非功實也。

translations.literal: Those who advance think it is because of accumulated seniority and worldly reputation—not real achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Those who advance think it is because of accumulated seniority and worldly reputation—not real achievement.

sentences.zh: 若謂不然，則當今之政未稱聖旨，此其征也。

translations.literal: If one says this is not so, then the government of today has not matched the sage intent—this is its sign.
translations.idiomatic: If one says this is not so, then the government of today has not matched your sage intent—this is its sign.

sentences.zh: 陛下禦今法為政將三十年，而功未日新，其咎安在？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has governed by the present law for nearly thirty years, yet achievement is not daily renewed—where lies the blame?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has governed by the present law for nearly thirty years, yet achievement is not daily renewed—where lies the blame?

sentences.zh: 古人有言：「琴瑟不調，甚者必改而更張。」

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: "When zither and lute are not in tune, in extreme cases one must change and restring them."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients had a saying: "When zither and lute are not in tune, in extreme cases one must change and restring them."

sentences.zh: 凡臣所言，誠政體之常，然古今異宜，所遇不同。

translations.literal: All that your servant speaks is truly the constant of the body of government; yet ancient and modern differ in suitability and what is encountered is different.
translations.idiomatic: All that your servant speaks is truly the constant of the body of government; yet ancient and modern differ in suitability and what is encountered is different.

sentences.zh: 陛下縱未得盡仰成之理，都委務於下，至如今事應奏禦者，蠲除不急，使要事得精可三分之二。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, even if not fully obtaining the principle of looking upward for completion, should wholly entrust affairs to those below; reaching to present affairs that should be memorialized to the throne, remove what is not urgent, so that important affairs may be made precise to about two-thirds.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, even if not fully obtaining the principle of looking upward for completion, should wholly entrust affairs to those below; as to present affairs that should be memorialized to the throne, remove what is not urgent, so that important affairs may be made precise to about two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 古者六卿分職，塚宰為師。

translations.literal: In antiquity the six ministers divided duties and the chief steward was their teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the six ministers divided duties and the chief steward was their teacher.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢已來，九列執事，丞相都總。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han onward, the nine ranks executed affairs and the chancellor gathered and oversaw all.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin and Han onward, the nine ranks executed affairs and the chancellor gathered and oversaw all.

sentences.zh: 今尚書制斷，諸卿奉成，于古制為重，事所不須，然今未能省並。

translations.literal: Now the Masters of Writing decide and cut off; the various ministers receive and complete—in the ancient system this is heavy and not needed for affairs; yet now one cannot yet reduce and merge.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Masters of Writing decide and cut off; the various ministers receive and complete—in the ancient system this is heavy and not needed for affairs; yet now one cannot yet reduce and merge.

sentences.zh: 可出眾事付外寺，使得專之，尚書為其都統，若丞相之為。

translations.literal: One may send out the multitude of affairs to outer offices, allowing them to decide exclusively; the Masters of Writing serve as their general overseer, as the chancellor did.
translations.idiomatic: One may send out the multitude of affairs to outer offices, allowing them to decide exclusively; the Masters of Writing serve as their general overseer, as the chancellor did.

sentences.zh: 惟立法創制，死生之斷，除名流徙，退免大事，及連度支之事，台乃奏處。

translations.literal: Only establishing law and creating institutions, decisions of life and death, removal of names and exile, great matters of dismissal and removal, and matters connected with revenue—the Secretariat then memorializes and decides.
translations.idiomatic: Only establishing law and creating institutions, decisions of life and death, removal of names and exile, great matters of dismissal and removal, and matters connected with revenue—the Secretariat then memorializes and decides.

sentences.zh: 其餘外官皆專斷之，歲終台閤課功校簿而已。

translations.literal: All other outer offices decide exclusively; at year's end the Secretariat and pavilion only assess achievement and verify registers.
translations.idiomatic: All other outer offices decide exclusively; at year's end the Secretariat and pavilion only assess achievement and verify registers.

sentences.zh: 此為九卿造創事始，斷而行之，尚書書主，賞罰繩之，其勢必愈考成司非而已。

translations.literal: Thus the nine ministers create and plan the beginning of affairs, decide and carry them out; the Masters of Writing record and preside, and reward and punishment bind them—the tendency must increasingly examine completion and office fault and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the nine ministers create and plan the beginning of affairs, decide and carry them out; the Masters of Writing record and preside, and reward and punishment bind them—the tendency must increasingly examine completion and office fault and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 於今親掌者動受成於上，上之所失，不得復以罪下，歲終事功不建，不知所責也。

translations.literal: As it is now, those who personally hold power constantly receive completion from above; the sovereign's failures cannot again be charged to those below; at year's end when achievement is not established, one does not know whom to blame.
translations.idiomatic: As it is now, those who personally hold power constantly receive completion from above; the sovereign's failures cannot again be charged to those below; at year's end when achievement is not established, one does not know whom to blame.

sentences.zh: 夫監司以法舉罪，獄官案劾盡實，法吏據辭守文，大較雖同，然至於施用，監司與夫法獄體宜小異。

translations.literal: Supervisors raise crimes by law; prison officials investigate and impeach to exhaust reality; law clerks rely on words and hold to text—broadly the same, yet as to application, supervisors and law prisons in substance should differ slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors raise crimes by law; prison officials investigate and impeach to exhaust reality; law clerks rely on words and hold to text—broadly the same, yet as to application, supervisors and law prisons in substance should differ slightly.

sentences.zh: 獄官唯實，法吏唯文，監司則欲舉大而略小。

translations.literal: Prison officials only [seek] reality; law clerks only [hold to] text; supervisors then wish to raise what is great and omit what is small.
translations.idiomatic: Prison officials only seek reality; law clerks only hold to text; supervisors then wish to raise what is great and omit what is small.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 夫細過微闕，謬妄之失，此人情之所必有，而悉糾以法，則朝野無全人，此所謂欲理而反亂者也。

translations.literal: Small faults and slight omissions, errors of mistake and recklessness—these are what human feeling necessarily has; yet if all are investigated by law, then in court and wild there are no whole men—this is what is called wishing to order yet instead creating disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Small faults and slight omissions, errors of mistake and recklessness—these are what human feeling necessarily has; yet if all are investigated by law, then in court and wild there are no whole men—this is what is called wishing to order yet instead creating disorder.

sentences.zh: 故善為政者綱舉而網疏，綱舉則所羅者廣，網疏則小必漏，所羅者廣則為政不苛，此為政之要也。

translations.literal: Therefore one who is good at governing raises the cord and leaves the net sparse; raising the cord then what is netted is broad, the net sparse then small things necessarily leak; what is netted broad then government is not harsh—this is the essential of governing.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one who is good at governing raises the cord and leaves the net sparse; raising the cord then what is netted is broad, the net sparse then small things necessarily leak; what is netted broad then government is not harsh—this is the essential of governing.

sentences.zh: 而自近世以來，為監司者，類大綱不振而微過必舉。

translations.literal: Yet from recent generations onward, those who serve as supervisors mostly do not raise the great cord yet always raise small faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from recent generations onward, those who serve as supervisors mostly do not raise the great cord yet always raise small faults.

sentences.zh: 微過不足以害政，舉之則微而益亂；

translations.literal: Small faults are not sufficient to harm government; raising them then makes things slight and increases disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Small faults are not sufficient to harm government; raising them then makes things slight and increases disorder;

sentences.zh: 大綱不振，則豪強橫肆，豪強橫肆，則百姓失職矣，此錯所急而倒所務之由也。

translations.literal: the great cord not raised, then the powerful and strong run rampant; the powerful and strong run rampant, then the hundred surnames lose their duties—this is the reason for mistaking what is urgent and inverting what is pursued.
translations.idiomatic: the great cord not raised, then the powerful and strong run rampant; the powerful and strong run rampant, then the common people lose their duties—this is the reason for mistaking what is urgent and inverting what is pursued.

sentences.zh: 今宜令有司反所常之政，使天下可善化。

translations.literal: Now one should order the relevant offices to reverse their usual government, so that the realm may be well transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Now one should order the relevant offices to reverse their usual government, so that the realm may be well transformed.

sentences.zh: 及此非難也，人主不善碎密之案，必責犯強舉尤之奏，當以盡公，則害政之奸自然禽矣。

translations.literal: Reaching this is not difficult; if the ruler does not favor fragmented and minute cases, but necessarily assigns blame for strong crimes and raises extreme memorials, taking exhausting the public good as the measure, then treacherous men who harm government will naturally be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching this is not difficult; if the ruler does not favor fragmented and minute cases, but necessarily assigns blame for strong crimes and raises extreme memorials, taking exhausting the public good as the measure, then treacherous men who harm government will naturally be captured.

sentences.zh: 夫大奸犯政而亂兆庶之罪者，類出富強，而豪富者其力足憚，其貨足欲，是以官長顧勢而頓筆。

translations.literal: Great treachery that violates government and disorders the crimes of the myriad multitude mostly comes from the rich and powerful; the rich and powerful have strength sufficient to inspire fear and goods sufficient for desire—therefore chief officials look to power and stop their brushes.
translations.idiomatic: Great treachery that violates government and disorders the myriad multitude mostly comes from the rich and powerful; the rich and powerful have strength sufficient to inspire fear and goods sufficient for desire—therefore chief officials look to power and stop their brushes.

sentences.zh: 下吏縱奸，懼所司之不舉，則謹密網以羅微罪。

translations.literal: Lower clerks indulge treachery; fearing that their superiors will not raise cases, they then carefully tighten the net to catch small crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Lower clerks indulge treachery; fearing that their superiors will not raise cases, they then carefully tighten the net to catch small crimes.

sentences.zh: 使奏劾相接，狀似盡公，而撓法不亮固已在其中矣。

translations.literal: Making memorials of impeachment follow one after another, the appearance seeming to exhaust the public good—yet bending law and not making it bright is already within it.
translations.idiomatic: Making memorials of impeachment follow one after another, the appearance seeming to exhaust the public good—yet bending law and not making it bright is already within it.

sentences.zh: 非徒無益于政體，清議乃由此而益傷。

translations.literal: Not merely without benefit to the body of government—pure discussion is thereby further harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Not merely without benefit to the body of government—pure discussion is thereby further harmed.

sentences.zh: 古人有言曰：「君子之過，如日之蝕焉。」

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: "The gentleman's fault is like an eclipse of the sun."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients had a saying: "The gentleman's fault is like an eclipse of the sun."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「過而能改」又曰「不貳過」。

translations.literal: Again they said, "Having fault yet able to reform"; again they said, "Do not repeat fault."
translations.idiomatic: They also said, "When one errs, one can reform"; and again, "Do not err twice in the same way."

sentences.zh: 凡此數者，皆是賢人君子不能無過之言也。

translations.literal: All these several are words that worthy men and gentlemen cannot be without fault.
translations.idiomatic: All these several are words that worthy men and gentlemen cannot be without fault.

sentences.zh: 苟不至於害政，則皆天網之所漏；

translations.literal: If they do not reach the point of harming government, then all are what Heaven's net leaks;
translations.idiomatic: If they do not reach the point of harming government, then all are what Heaven's net leaks;

sentences.zh: 所犯在甚泰，然後王誅所必加，此舉罪淺深之大例者也。

translations.literal: what is violated lies in being very excessive—only then is royal punishment necessarily applied; this is the great example of raising crimes shallow and deep.
translations.idiomatic: what is violated lies in being very excessive—only then is royal punishment necessarily applied; this is the great example of raising crimes shallow and deep.

sentences.zh: 故君子得全美以善事，不善者必夷戮以警眾，此為政誅赦之准式也。

translations.literal: Therefore gentlemen obtain full beauty to handle affairs well; those who are not good must be exterminated and executed to warn the multitude—this is the standard pattern of governing through punishment and pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore gentlemen obtain full beauty to handle affairs well; those who are not good must be exterminated and executed to warn the multitude—this is the standard pattern of governing through punishment and pardon.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 所謂賢人君子，苟不能無過，小疵不可以廢其身，而輒繩以法，則愧于明時。

translations.literal: The so-called worthy men and gentlemen, if they cannot be without fault, small blemishes may not be used to discard their persons—yet if one immediately binds them by law, one is ashamed before a bright age.
translations.idiomatic: The so-called worthy men and gentlemen, if they cannot be without fault, small blemishes may not be used to discard their persons—yet if one immediately binds them by law, one is ashamed before a bright age.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 雖有所犯，輕重甚殊，于士君子之心受責不同而名不異者，故不軌之徒得引名自方，以惑眾聽，因名可亂，假力取直，故清議益傷也。

translations.literal: Although there is violation, light and heavy are very different; in the hearts of scholar-gentlemen the blame received differs yet the name does not differ—therefore unprincipled fellows can cite the name to compare themselves, to confuse the multitude's hearing; by the name disorder may arise, borrowing power to obtain straightness; therefore pure discussion is further harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Although there is violation, light and heavy are very different; in the hearts of scholar-gentlemen the blame received differs yet the name does not differ—therefore unprincipled fellows can cite the name to compare themselves, to confuse the multitude's hearing; by the name disorder may arise, borrowing power to obtain straightness; therefore pure discussion is further harmed.

sentences.zh: 凡舉過彈違，將以肅風論而整世教，今舉小過，清議益穨。

translations.literal: Generally, raising faults and impeaching transgressions is meant to make wind and discussion solemn and put right worldly teaching; now raising small faults, pure discussion further declines.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, raising faults and impeaching transgressions is meant to make wind and discussion solemn and put right worldly teaching; now raising small faults, pure discussion further declines.

sentences.zh: 是以聖人深識人情而達政體，故其稱曰：「不以一眚掩大德。」

translations.literal: Therefore the sage deeply knows human feeling and penetrates the body of government; therefore his saying goes: "Do not with one fault cover great virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage deeply knows human feeling and penetrates the body of government; therefore his saying goes: "Do not with one fault cover great virtue."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「赦小過，舉賢才。」

translations.literal: " Again he said: "Pardon small faults, promote worthy talent."
translations.idiomatic: " Again he said: "Pardon small faults, promote worthy talent."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「無求備於一人。」

translations.literal: " Again he said: "Do not seek completeness in one man."
translations.idiomatic: " Again he said: "Do not seek completeness in one man."

sentences.zh: 故冕而前旒，充纊塞耳，意在善惡之報必取其尤，然後簡而不漏，大罪必誅，法禁易全也。

translations.literal: Therefore the cap with front tassels and padded earplugs stopping the ears—the intent is that in the reward of good and evil one must take the extreme; then simple yet not leaking, great crimes must be punished, and law and prohibition are easily kept whole.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the cap with front tassels and padded earplugs stopping the ears—the intent is that in the reward of good and evil one must take the extreme; then simple yet not leaking, great crimes must be punished, and law and prohibition are easily kept whole.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 害法在犯尤，而謹搜微過，何異放兕豹於公路，而禁鼠盜於隅隙。

translations.literal: Harm to law lies in violating extremes, yet carefully searching out small faults—what difference from releasing rhinoceroses and leopards on the public road yet forbidding mouse-thieves in corner cracks?
translations.idiomatic: Harm to law lies in violating extremes, yet carefully searching out small faults—what difference from releasing rhinoceroses and leopards on the public road yet forbidding mouse-thieves in corner cracks?

sentences.zh: 古人有言，「鈇鉞不用而刀鋸日弊，不可以為政」，此言大事緩而小事急也。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: "Axes and halberds are not used while knives and saws daily wear out—one cannot govern thus"; this speaks of great affairs being slow and small affairs being urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients had a saying: "Axes and halberds are not used while knives and saws daily wear out—one cannot govern thus"; this speaks of great affairs being slow and small affairs being urgent.

sentences.zh: 時政所失，少有此類，陛下宜反而求之，乃得所務也。

translations.literal: Among the failures of present government, there are somewhat of this kind; Your Majesty should turn and seek them—then one obtains what is pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Among the failures of present government, there are somewhat of this kind; Your Majesty should turn and seek them—then one obtains what is pursued.

sentences.zh: 夫權制不可以經常，政乖不可以守安，此言攻守之術異也。

translations.literal: Expedient institutions cannot be constant; government at odds cannot guard security—this speaks of the techniques of attack and defense being different.
translations.idiomatic: Expedient institutions cannot be constant; government at odds cannot guard security—this speaks of the techniques of attack and defense being different.

sentences.zh: 百姓雖愚，望不虛生，必因時而發。

translations.literal: Although the hundred surnames are foolish, hope is not born in vain—it must arise according to the time.
translations.idiomatic: Although the common people are foolish, hope is not born in vain—it must arise according to the time.

sentences.zh: 有因而發，則望不可奪；

translations.literal: When there is cause and it arises, then hope cannot be seized;
translations.idiomatic: When there is cause and it arises, then hope cannot be seized;

sentences.zh: 事變異前，則時不可違。

translations.literal: when affairs change differently from before, then the time cannot be violated.
translations.idiomatic: when affairs change differently from before, then the time cannot be violated.

sentences.zh: 明聖達政，應赴之速，不及下車，故能動合事機，大得人情。

translations.literal: The bright and sage who penetrate government respond with speed not reaching dismounting from the carriage; therefore they can move in accord with the occasion and greatly obtain human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The bright and sage who penetrate government respond with speed not reaching dismounting from the carriage; therefore they can move in accord with the occasion and greatly obtain human feeling.

sentences.zh: 昔魏武帝分離天下，使人役居戶，各在一方；

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Wei divided the realm, making men, corvée, dwellings, and households each in one region;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wu of Wei divided the realm, making men, corvée, dwellings, and households each in one region;

sentences.zh: 既事勢所須，且意有曲為，權假一時，以赴所務，非正典也。

translations.literal: both because affairs and power required it and because the intent had partial application, borrowing power for one time to rush to what was pursued—not the regular canon.
translations.idiomatic: both because affairs and power required it and because the intent had partial application, borrowing power for one time to rush to what was pursued—not the regular canon.

sentences.zh: 然逡巡至今，積年未改，百姓雖身丁其困，而私怨不生，誠以三方未悉蕩並，知時未可以求安息故也。

translations.literal: Yet hesitating until today, years accumulated without change, the hundred surnames although personally bearing its hardship yet private resentment did not arise—in truth because the three regions were not all swept and merged, knowing the time was not yet one in which rest could be sought.
translations.idiomatic: Yet hesitating until today, years accumulated without change, the common people although personally bearing its hardship yet private resentment did not arise—in truth because the three regions were not all swept and merged, knowing the time was not yet one in which rest could be sought.

sentences.zh: 是以甘役如歸，視險若夷。

translations.literal: Therefore they gladly accepted corvée as returning home and viewed peril as level ground.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore they gladly accepted corvée as returning home and viewed peril as level ground.

sentences.zh: 至於平吳之日，天下懷靜，而東南二方，六州郡兵，將士武吏，戍守江表，或給京城運漕，父南子北，室家分離，咸更不寧。

translations.literal: Reaching the day Wu was pacified, the realm cherished quiet; yet in the two southeastern regions, the six provinces' commandery troops, generals, soldiers, and military clerks garrisoned the lands south of the Yangzi or supplied transport to the capital—fathers south, sons north, households separated, all restless in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the day Wu was pacified, the realm cherished quiet; yet in the two southeastern regions, the six provinces' commandery troops, generals, soldiers, and military clerks garrisoned the lands south of the Yangzi or supplied transport to the capital—fathers south, sons north, households separated, all restless in rotation.

sentences.zh: 又不習水土，運役勤瘁，並有死亡之患，勢不可久。

translations.literal: Again they were unaccustomed to water and soil; transport corvée was toilsome and weary, and together there was the affliction of death—the posture could not long continue.
translations.idiomatic: Again they were unaccustomed to water and soil; transport corvée was toilsome and weary, and together there was the affliction of death—the posture could not long continue.

sentences.zh: 此宜大見處分，以副人望。

translations.literal: This should be greatly seen to and disposed, to match men's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: This should be greatly seen to and disposed, to match men's hopes.

sentences.zh: 魏氏錯役，亦應改舊。

translations.literal: Wei's mistaken corvée should also change the old ways.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's mistaken corvée should also change the old ways.

sentences.zh: 此二者各盡其理，然黔首感恩懷德，謳吟樂生必十倍於今也。

translations.literal: These two each exhaust their principle; then the black-haired people, grateful and cherishing virtue, singing and rejoicing in life, will necessarily be ten times what they are now.
translations.idiomatic: These two each exhaust their principle; then the common people, grateful and cherishing virtue, singing and rejoicing in life, will necessarily be ten times what they are now.

sentences.zh: 自董卓作亂以至今，近出百年，四海勤瘁，丁難極矣。

translations.literal: From Dong Zhuo's rebellion until now, nearly a hundred years have passed; the four seas have been toilsome and weary, and hardship for the people has reached its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: From Dong Zhuo's rebellion until now, nearly a hundred years have passed; the four seas have been toilsome and weary, and hardship for the people has reached its extreme.

sentences.zh: 六合渾並，始於今日，兆庶思寧，非虛望也。

translations.literal: The six directions merged as one begins from today; the myriad multitude think of peace—it is not an empty hope.
translations.idiomatic: The six directions merged as one begins from today; the myriad multitude think of peace—it is not an empty hope.

sentences.zh: 然古今異宜，所遇不同，誠亦未可以希遵在昔，放息馬牛。

translations.literal: Yet ancient and modern differ in suitability and what is encountered is different; in truth one also cannot yet hope to follow the past and release horses and oxen to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ancient and modern differ in suitability and what is encountered is different; in truth one also cannot yet hope to follow the past and release horses and oxen to rest.

sentences.zh: 然使受百役者不出其國，兵備待事其鄉，實在可為。

translations.literal: Yet if those who bear the hundred corvées do not leave their state and military preparations await affairs in their native district—in truth this can be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if those who bear the hundred corvées do not leave their state and military preparations await affairs in their native district—in truth this can be done.

sentences.zh: 縱復不得悉然為之，苟盡其理，可靜三分之二，吏役可不出千里之內。

translations.literal: Even if one cannot entirely do it so, if one exhausts its principle, two-thirds may be quieted and clerk corvée need not go outside a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one cannot entirely do it so, if one exhausts its principle, two-thirds may be quieted and clerk corvée need not go outside a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 但如斯而已，天下所蒙已不訾矣。

translations.literal: Merely thus and nothing more—the realm's benefit would already be beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Merely thus and nothing more—the realm's benefit would already be beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 政務多端，世事之未盡理者，難遍以疏舉，振領總綱，要在三條。

translations.literal: Government affairs have many branches; worldly affairs not yet fully ordered are hard to enumerate entirely in a memorial—shaking the collar and gathering the cord, the essential lies in three points.
translations.idiomatic: Government affairs have many branches; worldly affairs not yet fully ordered are hard to enumerate entirely in a memorial—shaking the collar and gathering the cord, the essential lies in three points.

sentences.zh: 凡政欲靜，靜在息役，息役在無為。

translations.literal: Generally, government wishes quiet; quiet lies in resting corvée; resting corvée lies in non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, government wishes quiet; quiet lies in resting corvée; resting corvée lies in non-action.

sentences.zh: 倉廩欲實，實在利農，利農在平糴。

translations.literal: Granaries wish to be filled; being filled lies in benefiting agriculture; benefiting agriculture lies in leveling grain purchases.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries wish to be filled; being filled lies in benefiting agriculture; benefiting agriculture lies in leveling grain purchases.

sentences.zh: 為政欲著信，著信在簡賢，簡賢在官久。

translations.literal: Governing wishes to show trust; showing trust lies in selecting the worthy; selecting the worthy lies in long tenure in office.
translations.idiomatic: Governing wishes to show trust; showing trust lies in selecting the worthy; selecting the worthy lies in long tenure in office.

sentences.zh: 官久非難也，連其班級，自非才宜，不得傍轉以終其課，則事善矣。

translations.literal: Long tenure in office is not difficult; linking their ranks, unless talent is unsuitable one may not sidestep transfer to complete their term—then affairs are well handled.
translations.idiomatic: Long tenure in office is not difficult; linking their ranks, unless talent is unsuitable one may not sidestep transfer to complete their term—then affairs are well handled.

sentences.zh: 平糴已有成制，其未備者可就周足，則穀積矣。

translations.literal: Leveling grain purchases already has an established system; what is not yet complete may be brought to fullness—then grain is stored.
translations.idiomatic: Leveling grain purchases already has an established system; what is not yet complete may be brought to fullness—then grain is stored.

sentences.zh: 無為匪他，卻功作之勤，抑似益而損之利。

translations.literal: Non-action is nothing else: repelling the diligence of construction works and restraining profits that seem beneficial yet are harmful.
translations.idiomatic: Non-action is nothing else: repelling the diligence of construction works and restraining profits that seem beneficial yet are harmful.

sentences.zh: 如斯而已，則天下靜矣。

translations.literal: Merely thus and nothing more, then the realm is quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Merely thus and nothing more, then the realm is quiet.

sentences.zh: 此三者既舉，雖未足以厚化，然可以為安有餘矣。

translations.literal: Once these three are raised, although not yet sufficient for thick transformation, yet one may be secure with surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Once these three are raised, although not yet sufficient for thick transformation, yet one may be secure with surplus.

sentences.zh: 夫王者之利，在生天地自然之財，農是也。

translations.literal: The profit of the king lies in producing Heaven and Earth's natural wealth—agriculture is this.
translations.idiomatic: The profit of the king lies in producing Heaven and Earth's natural wealth—agriculture is this.

sentences.zh: 所立為指於此，事誠有功益。

translations.literal: What is established and taken as the aim here—in affairs there is truly achievement and benefit.
translations.idiomatic: What is established and taken as the aim here—in affairs there is truly achievement and benefit.

sentences.zh: 苟或妨農，皆務所息，此悉似益而損之謂也。

translations.literal: If anything hinders agriculture, all such pursuits should be rested—this is all what is called seeming benefit yet being harm.
translations.idiomatic: If anything hinders agriculture, all such pursuits should be rested—this is all what is called seeming benefit yet being harm.

sentences.zh: 然今天下自有事所必須，不得止已，或用功甚少而所濟至重。

translations.literal: Yet in the realm today there are naturally affairs that must be done and cannot be stopped; or labor used is very little yet what is helped is extremely weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the realm today there are naturally affairs that must be done and cannot be stopped; or labor used is very little yet what is helped is extremely weighty.

sentences.zh: 目下為之，雖少有廢，而計終已大益。

translations.literal: Doing them at present, although slightly wasting some, yet calculating the end there is already great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Doing them at present, although slightly wasting some, yet calculating the end there is already great benefit.

sentences.zh: 農官有十百之利，及有妨害，在始似如未急，終作大患，宜逆加功，以塞其漸。

translations.literal: Agricultural offices have tenfold or hundredfold profit; when there is hindrance, at the beginning it seems not urgent, yet in the end it becomes a great affliction—one should in advance add effort to block its gradual spread.
translations.idiomatic: Agricultural offices have tenfold or hundredfold profit; when there is hindrance, at the beginning it seems not urgent, yet in the end it becomes a great affliction—one should in advance add effort to block its gradual spread.

sentences.zh: 如河、汴將合，沈萊苟善，則役不可息。

translations.literal: Such as when the Yellow River and Bian River are about to join—if Shen and Lai are well managed, then corvée cannot rest.
translations.idiomatic: Such as when the Yellow River and Bian River are about to join—if Shen and Lai are well managed, then corvée cannot rest.

sentences.zh: 諸如此類，亦不得已已。

translations.literal: All such as these—one also cannot help but stop.
translations.idiomatic: All such as these—one also cannot help but proceed.

sentences.zh: 然事患緩急，權計輕重，自非近如此類，准以為率，乃可興為，其餘皆務在靜息。

translations.literal: Yet affairs worry over urgency and slowness; expediently calculating light and heavy—unless near such as these, taking them as the measure, one may then undertake them; all the rest should pursue quiet and rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet affairs worry over urgency and slowness; expediently calculating light and heavy—unless near such as these, taking them as the measure, one may then undertake them; all the rest should pursue quiet and rest.

sentences.zh: 然能善算輕重，權審其宜，知可興可廢，甚難了也，自非上智遠才，不幹此任。

translations.literal: Yet to be able to well calculate light and heavy, expediently examine what is fitting, and know what may be undertaken and what may be abolished is very hard to complete—not unless supreme wisdom and far-reaching talent does one undertake this charge.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to be able to well calculate light and heavy, expediently examine what is fitting, and know what may be undertaken and what may be abolished is very hard to complete—not unless supreme wisdom and far-reaching talent does one undertake this charge.

sentences.zh: 夫創業之美，勳在垂統，使夫後世蒙賴以安。

translations.literal: The beauty of founding an enterprise: achievement lies in handing down the succession, making later generations rely upon it for security.
translations.idiomatic: The beauty of founding an enterprise: achievement lies in handing down the succession, making later generations rely upon it for security.

sentences.zh: 其為安也，雖昏猶明，雖愚若智。

translations.literal: Its being secure: though dark, still bright; though foolish, as if wise.
translations.idiomatic: Its being secure: though dark, still bright; though foolish, as if wise.

sentences.zh: 濟世功者，實在善化之為，要在靜國。

translations.literal: Achievement that saves the age lies in reality in good transformation; the essential lies in quieting the state.
translations.idiomatic: Achievement that saves the age lies in reality in good transformation; the essential lies in quieting the state.

sentences.zh: 至夫修飾宮署，凡諸作役務為恆傷過泰，不患不舉，此將來所不須于陛下而自能者也。

translations.literal: As to repairing and adorning palaces and offices—all various construction corvée constantly wound excessively, not fearing they will not be undertaken—this is what in the future Your Majesty need not concern himself with; it will come of itself.
translations.idiomatic: As to repairing and adorning palaces and offices—all various construction corvée constantly wound excessively, not fearing they will not be undertaken—this is what in the future Your Majesty need not concern yourself with; it will come of itself.

sentences.zh: 至於仰蒙前緒，所憑日月者，實在遺風系人心，余烈匡幼弱，而今勤所不須，以傷所憑。

translations.literal: As to relying upon and receiving the threads before, what is leaned upon like sun and moon lies in reality in surviving wind binding men's hearts and remaining vigor supporting the young and weak—yet now being diligent in what is not needed harms what is relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: As to relying upon and receiving the threads before, what is leaned upon like sun and moon lies in reality in surviving influence binding men's hearts and remaining vigor supporting the young and weak—yet now being diligent in what is not needed harms what is relied upon.

sentences.zh: 鈞此二者，何務孰急，陛下少垂恩回慮，詳擇所安，則大理盡矣。

translations.literal: Weighing these two, which pursuit is urgent, Your Majesty should slightly extend grace and turn consideration, carefully choosing what is secure—then the great principle is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing these two, which pursuit is urgent, Your Majesty should slightly extend grace and turn consideration, carefully choosing what is secure—then the great principle is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 世之私議，竊比陛下于孝文。

translations.literal: Private discussion in the world secretly compares Your Majesty to Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Private discussion in the world secretly compares Your Majesty to Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 臣以為聖德隆殺，將在乎後，不在當今。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that sage virtue's rise and decline will lie in what comes after, not in the present.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that sage virtue's rise and decline will lie in what comes after, not in the present.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 陛下龍飛鳳翔，應期踐阼，有創業之勳矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty soared as dragon and phoenix, responded to the season and ascended the throne—you already have the achievement of founding the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty soared as dragon and phoenix, responded to the season and ascended the throne—you already have the achievement of founding the enterprise.

sentences.zh: 掃滅強吳，奄征南海，又有之矣。

translations.literal: Sweeping away mighty Wu and suddenly campaigning to the Southern Sea—you have this too.
translations.idiomatic: Sweeping away mighty Wu and suddenly campaigning to the Southern Sea—you have this too.

sentences.zh: 以天子之貴，而躬行布衣之所難，孝儉之德，冠于百王，又有之矣。

translations.literal: With the Son of Heaven's nobility, yet personally practicing what common cloth is hard to do—filial and frugal virtue crowns the hundred kings; you have this too.
translations.idiomatic: With the Son of Heaven's nobility, yet personally practicing what common cloth is hard to do—filial and frugal virtue crowns the hundred kings; you have this too.

sentences.zh: 履宜無細，動成軌度，又有之矣。

translations.literal: Conducting what is fitting without detail, movement becoming rule and measure—you have this too.
translations.idiomatic: Conducting what is fitting in every detail, movement becoming rule and measure—you have this too.

sentences.zh: 若善當身之政，建籓屏之固，使晉代久長，後世仰瞻遺跡，校功考事，實與湯、武比靈斯，何孝文足雲！

translations.literal: If you manage well the government of your own person, establish the firmness of frontier screens, make the Jin age long endure, and later generations look up and gaze at surviving traces, comparing achievement and examining affairs—in reality comparing spiritual power with Tang and Wu—how is Emperor Xiaowen worth mentioning!
translations.idiomatic: If you manage well the government of your own reign, establish the firmness of frontier screens, make the Jin age long endure, and later generations look up and gaze at surviving traces, comparing achievement and examining affairs—in reality comparing spiritual power with Tang and Wu—how is Emperor Xiaowen worth mentioning!

sentences.zh: 臣之此言，非臣下褒上虛美常辭，其事實然。

translations.literal: Your servant's words here are not the minister below praising the sovereign with empty beauty and common phrases—the affair is indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's words here are not the minister below praising the sovereign with empty beauty and common phrases—the affair is indeed so.

sentences.zh: 若所以資為安之理，或未盡善，則恐良史書勳，不得遠盡弘美，甚可惜也。

translations.literal: If the principle by which one supports security is not yet fully good, then I fear good historians recording achievement will not be able remotely to exhaust grand beauty—very regrettable.
translations.idiomatic: If the principle by which one supports security is not yet fully good, then I fear good historians recording achievement will not be able remotely to exhaust grand beauty—very regrettable.

sentences.zh: 然不可使夫知政之士得參聖慮，經年少久，終必有成。

translations.literal: Yet one cannot make those who know government obtain participation in sage consideration; after years, little by little, in the end there will certainly be achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one cannot make those who know government obtain participation in sage consideration; after years, little by little, in the end there will certainly be achievement.

sentences.zh: 願陛下少察臣言。

translations.literal: He wishes Your Majesty slightly to examine your servant's words.
translations.idiomatic: He asks Your Majesty slightly to examine your servant's words.

sentences.zh: 又論肉刑，見《刑法志》。

translations.literal: He also discussed mutilating punishments; see the Treatise on Punishments and Law.
translations.idiomatic: His further memorial on restoring mutilating punishments is recorded in the Treatise on Punishments and Law.

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「得表陳封國之制，宜如古典，任刑齊法，宜復肉刑，及六州將士之役，居職之宜，諸所陳聞，具知卿之乃心為國也。

translations.literal: An edict replied that the memorial on enfeoffment following ancient canons, on restoring corporal punishment to align the laws, on service obligations for the six provinces, and on tenure in office had all been received, and that the throne fully knew his heart was set on the good of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered, "I have received your memorial on princely fiefdoms after the ancient pattern, on restoring corporal punishment to unify the law, on service obligations for the six provinces, and on tenure in office. In every point I see how wholly you devote yourself to the realm.

sentences.zh: 動靜數以聞。」

translations.literal: Report your movements and decisions frequently to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Keep me informed as matters develop."

sentences.zh: 元康初，從准南王允入朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang, he followed Prince of Huainan Yun to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuankang era he accompanied Prince Yun of Huainan to the capital; the received text miswrites the river name Huai.

sentences.zh: 會誅楊駿，頌屯衛殿中，其夜，詔以頌為三公尚書。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Jun was executed; Song garrisoned and guarded inside the halls, and that night an edict made Song Masters of Writing for the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun was put to death Liu Song held the palace watch, and that same night the emperor named him director of the Three Excellencies section of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 又上疏論律令事，為時論所美。

translations.literal: Again he submitted a memorial discussing statutes and ordinances matters, and was praised by contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: A further memorial on statutes and ordinances drew admiration across the court.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉吏部尚書，建九班之制，欲令百官居職希遷，考課能否，明其賞罰。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, establishing the nine-ranks system, wishing to cause the hundred officials in office to hope rarely for promotion, examine and assess ability or inability, and clarify their rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In time he became director of personnel and framed a nine-grade scheme meant to keep officials in post longer, grade their performance, and make rewards and sanctions transparent.

sentences.zh: 賈郭專朝，仕者欲速，竟不施行。

translations.literal: The Jia and Guo cliques monopolized court; office-seekers desired speed, and in the end it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: With the Jia and Guo factions dominating the government and every careerist demanding rapid promotion, the reform was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫之害張華也，頌哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao of Lun harmed Zhang Hua, Song wept for him very bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Lun of Zhao murdered Zhang Hua, Liu Song mourned him with wrenching grief.

sentences.zh: 聞華子得逃，喜曰：「茂先，卿尚有種也！」

translations.literal: Hearing that Hua's son had been able to escape, he joyfully said: "Maoxian, you still have seed!"
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhang Hua's son had escaped, he cried with relief, "Maoxian, your line survives yet!"

sentences.zh: 倫党張林聞之，大怒，憚頌持正而不能害也。

translations.literal: Lun partisan Zhang Lin heard it, was greatly angry, feared Song's upholding rectitude and could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin, a partisan of Prince Lun, heard this and fumed, yet dared not strike Liu Song down because his integrity commanded respect.

sentences.zh: 孫秀等推崇倫功，宜加九錫，百僚莫敢異議。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu and others extolled Lun's achievements and said the nine bestowals ought to be added; the hundred officials none dared a different opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu and his clique praised Prince Lun's merits and pressed for the nine insignia of usurpation, and not a minister dared dissent.

sentences.zh: 頌獨曰：「昔漢之錫魏，魏之錫晉，皆一時之用，非可通行。

translations.literal: Song alone said: "Formerly Han's bestowal on Wei, Wei's bestowal on Jin, were all one-time uses, not able to be generally applied.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song alone objected, "The Han grant to Wei and the Wei grant to Jin were one-off expedients, not a precedent to repeat at will.

sentences.zh: 今宗廟乂安，雖嬖後被退，勢臣受誅，周勃誅諸呂而尊孝文，霍光廢昌邑而奉孝宣，並無九錫之命。

translations.literal: Now the ancestral temple is peaceful; although the favorite empress was dismissed and powerful ministers received execution, Zhou Bo executed the various Lus and honored Emperor Xiaowen, Huo Guang deposed Changyi and served Emperor Xiaoxuan—neither had orders of the nine bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: The shrines are secure again: the favorite consort has been set aside and the overmighty ministers executed, as when Zhou Bo purged the Lü clan for Emperor Wen or Huo Guang deposed the king of Changyi for Emperor Xuan. Neither crisis was answered with the nine bestowals.

sentences.zh: 違舊典而習權變，非先王之制。

translations.literal: Violating old canons and practicing expedient shifts is not the former kings' system.
translations.idiomatic: To cast aside established rite and reach for such contrivances is alien to the way of the ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 九錫之議，請無所施。」

translations.literal: As for the discussion of the nine bestowals, I request nothing be applied."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that the proposal for the nine bestowals be dropped entirely."

sentences.zh: 張林積忿不已，以頌為張華之黨，將害之。

translations.literal: Zhang Lin piled up resentment without cease, took Song as Zhang Hua's faction, and was about to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin nursed a growing grudge, branded Liu Song a partisan of Zhang Hua, and plotted to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 孫秀曰：「誅張、裴已傷時望，不可復誅頌。」

translations.literal: Sun Xiu said: "Executing Zhang and Pei has already injured the age's expectation; we cannot again execute Song."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu warned him, "Executing Zhang Hua and Pei Xiu has already cost us the goodwill of the realm. Liu Song must not be killed as well."

sentences.zh: 林乃止。

translations.literal: Lin then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 於是以頌為光祿大夫，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Song was made Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, and pacing horses were set at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song was therefore appointed grand master of splendid carriage with the honor of dismounting rails before his gate.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒，使使者弔祭，賜錢二十萬、朝服一具，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill and died; envoys were sent to condole and sacrifice, granting two hundred thousand cash and one set of court dress; his posthumous name was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness. The court sent envoys to mourn him, gave two hundred thousand cash and a full set of court robes, and posthumously styled him Zhen, Upright.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎劉沈議，頌當時少輩，應贈開府。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Gentleman Liu Shen debated that Song, of the age's younger generation, ought to be posthumously gifted opening of a mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen of the palace secretariat argued that Liu Song, among the foremost men of his generation, deserved the posthumous privilege of a grand commander's establishment.

sentences.zh: 孫秀素恨之，不聽。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu long hated him and did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu, who had long detested Liu Shen, rejected the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 頌無子，養弟和子雍早卒，更以雍弟詡子𨻳為嫡孫，襲封，

translations.literal: Song had no sons; he had adopted his younger brother He's son Yong, who died early; he further took Yong's younger brother Xu's son Na as heir grandson, to inherit the fief,
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song left no sons. He had adopted Yong, son of his brother Liu He, but Yong died young, so the line passed to Na, son of Xu, Yong's younger brother, as heir grandson to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 永康元年，詔以頌誅賈謐督攝眾事有功，追封梁鄒縣侯，食邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, an edict because Song in executing Jia Mi and overseeing the multitude of affairs had merit, posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Liangzou county, with food households one thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongkang, Later an edict noted Liu Song's part in executing Jia Mi and steadying the government, posthumously creating him marquis of Liangzou with fifteen hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 頌弟彪字仲雅，參安東軍事。

translations.literal: Song's younger brother Biao, courtesy name Zhongya, was a staff adviser on Eastern Pacification military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song's younger brother Liu Biao, courtesy name Zhongya, served on the staff of the army of eastern pacification.

sentences.zh: 伐吳，獲張悌，累官積弩將軍。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Wu, he captured Zhang Ti, and by accumulated offices became General of the Crossbowmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Wu he took the Wu commander Zhang Ti prisoner and rose through several posts to general of the crossbowmen.

sentences.zh: 及武庫火，彪建計斷屋，得出諸寶器。

translations.literal: When the armory caught fire, Biao proposed a plan to cut off roofs, enabling the various precious implements to be brought out.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial armory burned, Liu Biao ordered sections of roof struck away so the stored weapons could be salvaged.

sentences.zh: 曆荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed through Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 次弟仲字世混，曆黃門郎、滎陽太守，未之官，卒。

translations.literal: The next younger brother Zhong, courtesy name Shihun, passed through Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Administrator of Xingyang; before going to office, he died.
translations.idiomatic: The next brother, Liu Zhong, courtesy name Shihun, held appointments as gentleman of the yellow gate and prefect of Xingyang but died before he could assume the latter post.

sentences.zh: 初，頌嫁女臨淮陳矯，矯本劉氏子，與頌近親，出養于姑，改姓陳氏。

translations.literal: Initially, Song married a daughter to Chen Jiao of Linhuai; Jiao was originally a Liu clan son, close kin to Song, given out in adoption to an aunt, and changed surname to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Song had given a daughter in marriage to Chen Jiao of Linhuai. Chen Jiao was born a Liu, a near kinsman of Liu Song, but had been adopted by an aunt and took the Chen surname.

sentences.zh: 中正劉友譏之，頌曰：「舜後姚虞、陳田本同根系，而世皆為婚，禮律不禁。

translations.literal: Rectifier Liu You ridiculed it; Song said: "After Shun, Yao Yu and Chen Tian were originally the same root system, yet generations all made marriage; rites and statutes did not forbid.
translations.idiomatic: The local rectifier Liu You objected. Liu Song replied, "The houses of Yao, Yu, Chen, and Tian stem from a single Shun-line ancestry, yet they have intermarried for generations without the code forbidding it.

sentences.zh: 今與此同義，為婚可也。」

translations.literal: Now with this it is the same meaning; to make marriage is permissible."
translations.idiomatic: Our case falls under the same principle, so the match is lawful."

sentences.zh: 友方欲列上，為陳騫所止，故得不劾。

translations.literal: You was just about to list and report upward, but was stopped by Chen Qian, therefore was able to avoid impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu You was preparing a formal denunciation when Chen Qian intervened, so no charges were filed.

sentences.zh: 頌問明法掾陳默、蔡畿曰：「鄉里誰最屈？」

translations.literal: Song asked law clerks Chen Mo and Cai Ji, saying: "In the village who is most wronged?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song asked his law clerks Chen Mo and Cai Ji, "Who in our district has been wronged worst?"

sentences.zh: 二人俱云：「劉友屈。」

translations.literal: The two together said: "Liu You is wronged."
translations.idiomatic: Both answered, "Liu You."

sentences.zh: 頌作色呵之，畿曰：「友以私議冒犯明府為非，然鄉里公論稱屈。」

translations.literal: Song changed color and shouted at them; Ji said: "You, by private discussion offending the enlightened prefect, was wrong, yet the village's public opinion calls him wronged."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song flushed and rebuked them. Cai Ji ventured, "Liu You was wrong to press a private grudge against your honor, yet public opinion still calls him the injured party."

sentences.zh: 友辟公府掾、尚書郎、黃沙御史。

translations.literal: You was summoned as clerk in the princely offices, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and Cavalier Investigator at Huangsha.
translations.idiomatic: Liu You went on to serve as princely clerk, gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and cavalier investigator at the Huangsha prison.

sentences.zh: 李重

translations.literal: Li Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong.

sentences.zh: 李重字茂曾，江夏鐘武人也。

translations.literal: Li Zhong, courtesy name Maozeng, was a man of Zhongwu in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong, courtesy name Maozeng, was a native of Zhongwu in Jiangxia commandery.

sentences.zh: 父景，秦州刺史、都亭定侯。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Inspector of Qinzhou, Marquis Ding of Duting.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Jing had been inspector of Qinzhou and marquis Ding of Duting.

sentences.zh: 重少好學，有文辭；

translations.literal: Zhong in youth loved learning and had literary phrasing;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong loved learning from youth and wrote with polish;

sentences.zh: 早孤，與群弟居，以友愛著稱。

translations.literal: he was early orphaned, dwelt with his band of younger brothers, and was noted for friendly love.
translations.idiomatic: orphaned early, he kept house with his younger brothers and was famed for fraternal devotion.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為本國中正，遜讓不行。

translations.literal: At the capping age he became rectifier of his native state, declined yielding and did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: When capped he was offered the rectifier's post for his home principality but modestly refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 後為始平王文學，上疏陳九品曰：先王議制，以時因革，因革之理，唯變所適。

translations.literal: Later he became literary scholar to Prince Shiping of the Wei and submitted a memorial stating on the nine ranks: Former kings deliberated on institutions, reforming with the times; the principle of following and changing lies solely in adapting to what fits.
translations.idiomatic: He later became tutor in letters to the prince of Shiping and memorialized on the nine-rank system as follows: The ancient kings shaped institutions by reforming them to suit the age; the logic of continuity and change is simply to adapt to what the times require.

sentences.zh: 九品始於喪亂，軍中之政，誠非經國不刊之法也。

translations.literal: The nine ranks began in mourning and disorder, as military-camp administration—truly not the immutable law for governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: The nine-rank system arose amid the chaos of war as a product of military administration, and is certainly not an immutable statute for governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 且其檢防轉碎，征刑失實，故朝野之論，僉謂驅動風俗，為弊已甚。

translations.literal: Moreover its inspection and restraint grew ever more fragmented, and recruitment by punishment lost touch with reality; hence opinion in court and countryside alike agreed that it stirred up custom and morals, and the harm is already very grave.
translations.idiomatic: Its oversight grew ever more fragmented and its gradings ever less truthful, so court and countryside alike hold that it has warped public morals and done grave harm.

sentences.zh: 而至於議改，又以為疑。

translations.literal: Yet when it comes to discussing reform, people again hold doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when reform is proposed, doubts arise again.

sentences.zh: 臣以革法創制，當先盡開塞利害之理，舉而錯之，使體例大通而無否滯亦未易故也。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that in reforming law and creating institutions, one ought first fully to exhaust the principles of what opens and blocks, benefits and harms, raise it and apply it, so that the system's overall pattern is broadly coherent without obstruction and stagnation—yet to change this is also not easy.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that reforming institutions requires first laying out what opens or blocks the way, what helps or harms the state, and applying that design so the whole system flows without obstruction—yet such a change is not easily made.

sentences.zh: 古者諸侯之治，分土有常，國有定主，人無異望，卿大夫世祿，仕無出位之思，臣無越境之交，上下體固，人德歸厚。

translations.literal: In antiquity under the feudal lords' rule, apportioned land had fixed bounds, states had settled masters, people had no divergent hopes, ministers and grandees enjoyed hereditary emoluments, in office there was no thought of overstepping rank, ministers had no dealings across boundaries; upper and lower were structurally solid, and human virtue returned to depth.
translations.idiomatic: Under the feudal lords of antiquity, fiefs had fixed boundaries and states had settled rulers; the people entertained no divided loyalties. Grandees and ministers held hereditary stipends, officials did not scheme beyond their stations, and subjects did not cultivate ties across borders. Authority and obligation were firmly knit, and men returned to solid virtue.

sentences.zh: 秦反斯道，罷侯置守，風俗淺薄，自此來矣。

translations.literal: Qin reversed this Way, abolishing feudal lords and establishing commandery governors; shallow and thin custom, from this it came.
translations.idiomatic: Qin overturned that order, abolishing feudal lords and appointing commandery governors, and the erosion of moral custom began then.

sentences.zh: 漢革其弊，斟酌周、秦，並建侯守，亦使分土有定，而牧司必各舉賢，貢士任之鄉議，事合聖典，比蹤三代。

translations.literal: Han reformed its evils, weighing Zhou and Qin, jointly establishing marquisates and governors, also making apportioned lands fixed; regional overseers each had to recommend the worthy, and presenting scholars relied on local opinion—the matter accorded with sage canons and traced the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Han remedied those abuses by blending Zhou and Qin precedents, combining enfeoffed domains with commandery administration and fixing territorial boundaries. Regional overseers had to recommend talent, and presented scholars rested on local reputation—in keeping with the sage canon and echoing the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 方今聖德之隆，光被四表，兆庶顒顒，欣睹太平。

translations.literal: Now your sagely virtue is lofty, its light covering the four quarters; the myriad people look up with eager faces, joyfully beholding great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Today your sage virtue shines to the four quarters, and the common people look up in hope, eager to witness the age of peace.

sentences.zh: 然承魏氏凋弊之跡，人物播越，仕無常朝，人無定處，郎吏蓄於軍府，豪右聚於都邑，事體駁錯，與古不同。

translations.literal: Yet inheriting the traces of Wei decline and exhaustion, people and things were scattered far and wide; office had no fixed court, men had no fixed dwelling. Gentleman clerks were stored in military offices, great magnates gathered in capital cities—the actual situation was tangled and mixed, unlike antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet we inherit the ruin left by Wei: families and reputations scattered, no fixed court for service, no fixed homes for men. Clerkships pile up in military headquarters while great families cluster in the capital—a tangle of affairs unlike anything in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 謂九品既除，宜先開移徙，聽相並就。

translations.literal: I say once the nine ranks are abolished, one should first open movement and migration, allowing people to combine and settle together.
translations.idiomatic: Once the nine ranks are abolished, migration should be encouraged first so people may relocate and merge communities as they choose.

sentences.zh: 且明貢舉之法，不濫於境外，則冠帶之倫將不分而自均，即土斷之實行矣。

translations.literal: Moreover clarify the law of tribute and recommendation, not extending beyond the borders, then the rank of gentry by cap and sash will not need to be divided but will naturally balance—that is the actual implementation of fixing land and severing ties across borders.
translations.idiomatic: And if recommendation procedures are clarified so they do not extend beyond local boundaries, then the gentry ranks will settle themselves without forced division—that is true land registration and territorial alignment.

sentences.zh: 又建樹官司，功在簡久。

translations.literal: Further, in establishing government offices, the merit lies in simplicity and longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Government offices should likewise be organized, and here the virtue lies in simplicity and stability over time.

sentences.zh: 階級少，則人心定；

translations.literal: When ranks are few, then people's hearts are settled;
translations.idiomatic: Fewer ranks settle people's minds;

sentences.zh: 久其事，則政化成而能否著，此三代所以直道而行也。

translations.literal: when the affairs endure long, then governance transforms and ability or inability becomes manifest—this is why the Three Dynasties could travel the straight Way.
translations.idiomatic: long tenure in office lets government take root and talent show itself—that is how the Three Dynasties walked the straight path of rule.

sentences.zh: 以為選例九等，當今之要，所宜施用也。

translations.literal: I hold that a selection regulation of nine grades is the urgent matter of the present age, what ought to be applied and used.
translations.idiomatic: A nine-grade selection scheme is the urgent need of our day and should be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 聖王知天下之難，常從事于其易，故寄隱括于閭伍，則邑屋皆為有司。

translations.literal: The sage king knows the realm's difficulties and always works at what is easy; therefore he lodges oversight in neighborhood groups, and then hamlets and dwellings all become the charge of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings know the realm is hard to govern and begin with what is easy; therefore they lodge oversight in local communities so that every village becomes the concern of its officials.

sentences.zh: 若任非所由，事非所核，則雖竭聖智，猶不足以贍其事。

translations.literal: If appointment is not from the proper channel, and affairs are not verified at the proper level, then even exhausting sage wisdom is still not enough to supply those affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If appointments are not made through proper channels and affairs are not checked at the proper level, then even the utmost sage wisdom cannot sustain the work.

sentences.zh: 由此而觀，誠令二者既行，即人思反本，修之于鄉，華競自息，而禮讓日隆矣。

translations.literal: From this perspective, if these two measures are truly implemented, then people will think to return to their roots, cultivate themselves in the countryside, ostentatious rivalry will naturally cease, and courtesy and yielding will daily rise.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed thus, if both measures were truly carried out, men would turn back to their roots, cultivate virtue in their home villages, flashy competition would die away of itself, and courtesy and yielding would flourish day by day.

sentences.zh: 遷太子舍人，轉尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Household Gentleman to the Heir Apparent, then transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to household gentleman to the heir apparent and then to gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時太中大夫恬和表陳便宜，稱漢孔光、魏徐幹等議，使王公已下制奴婢限數，及禁百姓賣田宅。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Palace Grandee Tian He memorialized convenient matters, citing Han Kong Guang, Wei Xu Gan and others' debates, causing kings and dukes downward to regulate slave and maidservant limit numbers, and forbidding the hundred surnames to sell fields and houses.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Palace Grandee Tian He then submitted a utilitarian memorial, invoking Han debates led by Kong Guang and Wei discussions by Xu Gan, urging caps on slaveholding for the nobility downward and a ban on commoners' sale of land and houses.

sentences.zh: 中書啟可，屬主者為條制。

translations.literal: The palace secretariat opened and approved, charging the competent authorities to make articles and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The palace secretariat endorsed the plan and told the responsible agencies to draft implementing rules.

sentences.zh: 重奏曰：先王之制，士農工商有分，不遷其業，所以利用厚生，各肆其力也。

translations.literal: Zhong memorialized saying: The former kings' system had divisions among scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants; they did not shift their occupations—this was the means to profit from things and enrich life, each exerting his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong replied in a memorial: Under the institutions of the ancient kings, scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants each had their allotted station and did not change trades, so that resources might be put to use, livelihoods enriched, and every man apply his labor where it belonged.

sentences.zh: 《周官》以土均之法，經其土地井田之制，而辨其五物九等貢賦之序，然後公私制定，率土均齊。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou used the method of equalizing land to regulate the system of land and well-fields, and distinguished the order of tribute and levies in five goods and nine grades; only then were public and private fixed, and all within the land made even.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou employed land-equalization to lay out the well-field system, ranked tribute and taxes across the nine grades of the five categories of goods, and only then fixed what belonged to the state and to private holders, making the realm as a whole evenly ordered.

sentences.zh: 自秦立阡陌，建郡縣，而斯制已沒。

translations.literal: From Qin establishing field paths and building commanderies and counties, this system already perished.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qin opened the grid of private fields and replaced feudal domains with commanderies and counties, that system was lost forever.

sentences.zh: 降及漢、魏，因循舊跡，王法所峻者，唯服物車器有貴賤之差，令不僭擬以亂尊卑耳。

translations.literal: Descending to Han and Wei, they followed the old tracks; what the royal law strictly enforced was only that clothing, goods, carts, and implements had distinctions of noble and base, ordering that none usurp and imitate to disorder honor and lowliness.
translations.idiomatic: Through Han and Wei alike, government followed the old path: royal law was strict chiefly in dress, furnishings, carriages, and utensils, forbidding anyone to imitate above his rank and thereby blur the hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 至於奴婢私產，則實皆未嘗曲為之立限也。

translations.literal: As for slaves and maidservants and private property, in truth none ever bent to establish limits for them.
translations.idiomatic: As for slaves and private wealth, no dynasty ever seriously imposed fixed limits upon them.

sentences.zh: 八年《己巳詔書》申明律令，諸士卒百工以上，所服乘皆不得違制。

translations.literal: The eighth-year Jisi Edict clarified statutes and ordinances: all soldiers and craftsmen from that rank upward—what they wore and rode must not violate regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The jisi edict of the eighth year spelled out the law anew: soldiers, artisans, and all ranks above them were forbidden to wear or ride beyond what their station allowed.

sentences.zh: 若一縣一歲之中，有違犯者三家，洛陽縣十家已上，官長免。
